items.title: The library of the future: Services, agility and a functional identity continuum
items.abstract: Abstract Academic libraries are currently undergoing fundamental change. Digitisation, open access, research data management, artificial intelligence, changing learning and research practices, and the transformation of the publishing system are broadening their remit whilst simultaneously raising users’ expectations of them. In international professional discourse, this development is often described as a transition from a collection-centred library to one that is more service- and workflow-oriented. (Dempsey and Malpas 2018; Pinfield, Cox and Rutter 2017; Lavoie and Bryant 2026) This brings with it new opportunities. Libraries can develop new services, align themselves more closely with research and learning processes, and expand their role as an infrastructure for academic communication. At the same time, an institutional tension is emerging. Library services are increasingly breaking down into individual services, some of which could also be provided by other organisational units. This makes the question of what enables the library to remain recognisable as a library all the more pressing. This article proposes framing this question using the concept of the ‘functional identity continuum’. This does not imply a static adherence to traditional forms, but rather an interconnection between collection, selection, cataloguing, contextualisation, access, space, preservation, outreach and institutional responsibility. From this perspective, the library of the future remains a plausible institutional form only if it sustainably integrates new services and anchors them to a core library function.

items.title: The mediating role of self-efficacy in the relationships of technophilia and positive emotional experience with perceived learning effectiveness in AI-supported EFL education
items.abstract: Abstract Despite the increasing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into English as a Foreign Language (EFL) education, the psychological mechanisms linking learners’ technological dispositions and emotional experiences to perceived learning effectiveness remain undertheorized and empirically underexplored. This study examined whether self-efficacy served as a statistical mediator in the relationships of technophilia and positive emotional experience with perceived learning effectiveness in AI-supported EFL education. A cross-sectional survey was conducted involving 234 students enrolled in English-language courses at a private college of health sciences. Adapted multi-item scales on technophilia, positive emotional experience, self-efficacy, and perceived learning effectiveness were administered. Structural equation modeling with bootstrapping (5000 resamples) was used to examine direct and indirect associations. Self-efficacy demonstrated the strongest direct association with perceived learning effectiveness (β = 0.375, p = 0.001). Positive emotional experience was strongly associated with self-efficacy (β = 0.624, p < 0.001), and its indirect association with perceived learning effectiveness through self-efficacy was significant (β = 0.234, 95% CI [0.128, 0.351]). Technophilia was also positively associated with self-efficacy (β = 0.307, p = 0.002), and its indirect association with perceived learning effectiveness through self-efficacy was significant. The findings were consistent with self-efficacy partially mediating both relationships. These findings suggest that learners’ confidence in managing AI-supported tasks plays an important role in linking affective dispositions to perceived effectiveness appraisals. The study contributes to computer-assisted language learning (CALL) research by clarifying how positive orientation toward AI-supported technologies, emotional experience, and efficacy beliefs jointly relate to learners’ perceptions of effective AI-supported language learning. Pedagogically, the findings suggest that progressively scaffolded practice and mastery-oriented AI tasks may strengthen self-efficacy and improve learners’ perceived effectiveness in AI-supported EFL environments.

items.title: The ovarian cellular ecosystem in polycystic ovary syndrome: from cellular heterogeneity to clinical relevance
items.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is one of the most biologically heterogeneous disorders in reproductive endocrinology, extending far beyond the classical features of hyperandrogenism, ovulatory dysfunction, and polycystic ovarian morphology. Although substantial progress has been made in defining the endocrine, metabolic, genetic, epigenetic, and inflammatory mechanisms associated with PCOS, these processes have largely been investigated independently, and their contribution to the marked clinical and biological heterogeneity of the disorder remains incompletely understood. Recent advances in cellular-resolution biology, including single-cell and single-nucleus transcriptomics, spatial omics, and multimodal molecular profiling, together with computational systems biology, enable increasingly detailed characterization of cellular states, spatial organization, and molecular relationships within the ovarian-follicular environment. In this Review, we use the ovarian cellular ecosystem as an operational systems framework to test whether PCOS-associated abnormalities observed in individual ovarian and follicular compartments form reproducible higher-order patterns of multicellular organization. The framework is organized across five measurable domains: cellular composition and states, intercellular signaling relationships, spatial niche organization, cross-compartment molecular coupling, and systemic-ovarian coupling. Current direct human cellular-resolution evidence remains sparse and compartment-specific. Available studies support altered molecular and cellular states within selected ovarian and follicular compartments more strongly than coordinated, spatially organized, or progressive ecosystem-wide remodeling. We critically evaluate how cellular-resolution, spatial, multi-omics, computational and artificial intelligence approaches can be used to test these ecosystem-level hypotheses, explicitly distinguishing direct measurement from computational inference and identifying the validation required for functional or causal interpretation. Finally, we discuss the translational implications of this framework for biologically informed patient stratification, ecosystem-derived biomarker discovery, mechanism-informed therapeutic development, and precision reproductive endocrinology. By integrating current evidence within a falsifiable framework, this Review defines measurable features and validation criteria for testing ovarian ecosystem organization in PCOS and identifies the critical evidence gaps that future cellular-resolution, spatial, and multi-omic studies must address. This provides a practical roadmap for determining whether reproducible ovarian ecosystem states can improve biological stratification, biomarker discovery, or therapeutic target identification beyond compartment-specific abnormalities and established systemic and clinical determinants.

items.title: The Paradox of Algorithmic Sycophancy: Sycophancy in Large Language Models and the Limits of AI-Mediated Knowledge Reconstruction in the Metacognitive Creative Destruction Model
items.abstract: The Metacognitive Creative Destruction (MCD) model approaches educational innovation as a perpetual spiral process. Contradiction (accumulated cognitive conflicts that resist interpretation), activates Metacognitive Capacity, enabling Destructive Unlearning Propensity, the conscious abandonment of outdated mental schemas, which in turn enables Creative Reconstruction Ability, and ultimately, new knowledge. In the model’s empirical validation with 1,498 teachers, a critical finding emerged: AI Augmentation Intensity (AIA) predicted Metacognitive Capacity (MC) and Creative Reconstruction Ability (CRA), but not Destructive Unlearning Propensity (DUP).This article argues that this finding is not accidental, but reflects an inherent weakness of modern AI systems, and more specifically, the tendency toward AI Sycophancy. Models trained with reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) tend to avoid disagreements and be likable to the user, preventing the individual from experiencing cognitive conflicts, perpetuating their already formed beliefs at the expense of scientific accuracy.Therefore, in an environment of “algorithmic flattery”, the necessary contradictions that trigger unlearning are not produced. Based on the MCD model, it is concluded that the absence of unlearning, that is, the deliberate and conscious abandonment of outdated beliefs, mental models and practices, makes the reconstruction of knowledge absolutely superficial and thus, algorithmically condescending interaction does not produce deep and authentic knowledge, regardless of AI Augmentation Intensity.

items.title: THE PARTICLE THAT KEPT MOVING: A SWARM-EQUATION BIOGRAPHY OF SATISH GAJAWADA (IIT ROORKEE ALUMNUS). INERTIA, MEMORY, GUIDANCE AND WONDER IN FOURTEEN YEARS OF INDEPENDENT ARTIFICIAL-INTELLIGENCE RESEARCH
items.abstract: Most biographies follow a life through time. This one follows a life through an equation. Satish Gajawada, an Integrated Dual Degree (B.Tech + M.Tech) graduate of the Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee (2012), has spent fourteen years as an independent researcher who gives names, structure and heart to ideas in artificial intelligence: Excellent AI (EAI), Very Highly Advanced AI (VHAAI), Out of the Box AI (OBAI), a society (ISVHAAI), a family of value-themed swarm algorithms, thirteen theories of human purpose, a 108-right taxonomy of human rights, and a lifelong “thesis” supervised by his parents and GOD. Reading the particle swarm update rule as a metaphor for a research life, this article identifies four forces (inertia, personal best, global best and exploration) and one outcome: a position update that, in 2026, turned decisively toward testing and open disclosure. Drawing on eight source documents, with each statement attributed to a published work, a manuscript or the subject’s own account, we show that a reproducible genetic-algorithm and PSO experiment found a fairness weight that cut a demographic-parity gap from 0.121 to 0.016 for 1.9 points of accuracy, and a gentler weight that improved accuracy and fairness together. Itemised output rose from one entry in 2012 to twelve in 2026. We conclude that Gajawada is a builder of human-centred vocabulary and institutions, a grateful son, a joyful experimenter and a candid author, and that his life offers every learner a portable update rule: keep your direction, honour your best, listen to your guides, stay curious, and keep moving.

items.title: THE ROLE OF AI-POWERED DUOLINGO AND ELSA SPEAK APPS IN REDUCING SPEAKING ANXIETY AMONG ENGLISH LEARNERS IN PRIVATE UNIVERSITIES OF DHAKA, BANGLADESH
items.abstract: This study has explored the influence of speaking anxiety as a major obstacle for English as foreign language learners (EFL) in their non-native environment like in the private universities in Dhaka, Bangladesh. With the up rise of Artificial Intelligence, English language learning applications have incorporated AI-based features to enhance the learning experience. This finding examined how AI-supported speaking apps, in this instance, Duolingo and ELSA Speak, reduce speaking anxiety and increase learners' confidence, fluency and speaking skills through AI-driven personalized feedback, gamified interaction and adaptive learning. This research used mixed-method approach, which included qualitative and quantitative methods to provide comprehensive insights and understanding. The results of the study pointed to the effectiveness of AI-based language learning apps in creating a supportive language-learning atmosphere, enhancing the learning process and reducing stress levels when practicing oral communication. The results of this study could contribute to the understanding of how AI-based app-based learning can be incorporated in the university curriculum and evidence-based recommendations for teachers, educational technology designers and policy makers.

items.title: THE ROLE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN ENGLISH LANGUAGE LEARNING: OPPORTUNITIES, CHALLENGES, AND PEDAGOGICAL IMPLICATIONS
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly influencing Englishlanguage learning by providing personalized instruction, immediate feedback,interactive communication, and opportunities for independent practice. This paperexamines the potential benefits and challenges of integrating AI technologies intoEnglish as a Foreign Language (EFL) learning. The study adopts a literature reviewapproach and draws on existing empirical research, systematic reviews, andinternational educational guidance. The reviewed literature suggests that AI-supportedlearning can contribute to language development, particularly by providing writingfeedback, facilitating conversational practice, and supporting learner engagement.However, the effectiveness of these technologies depends on the quality of AIgenerated feedback, learners’ digital literacy, appropriate pedagogical guidance, andresponsible use. Potential challenges include inaccurate information, excessivedependence on AI, academic integrity concerns, and data privacy risks. The paperargues that AI should complement rather than replace teachers and meaningful humaninteraction. It concludes that the responsible integration of AI into English languageeducation requires clear learning objectives, critical evaluation of AI-generated content,and a balanced combination of technological tools and teacher-led instruction.

items.title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Treatment Planning in Physical and Rehabilitation Medicine
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Individualized rehabilitation plans are crucial for maximizing clinical outcomes. Generative artificial intelligence (AI), particularly large language models (LLMs), which can generate new content based on large knowledge bases, could improve personalized rehabilitation. This systematic review aimed to assess accuracy and application of LLMs in rehabilitation. DESIGN: A systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus until February 2026. The PICO included LLMs (P), their use in rehabilitation planning (I), comparison with expert opinion or other AI systems (e.g., machine learning, deep learning, or CDSS) (C), the ability to generate appropriate rehabilitation plans and compliance with expert clinicians or clinical practice guidelines (O). Studies involving non-generative AI were excluded. Methodological quality was assessed with JBI tools. Data extraction was performed by two reviewers; a third resolved conflicts. RESULTS: Nine studies met inclusion criteria. Concordance with expert opinion varied, reaching 98.75% after an expert advisory board reviewed AI-generated statements. In musculoskeletal and cardiovascular rehabilitation, LLMs demonstrated alignment with guidelines. However, the included studies reported hallucinations, underscoring the necessity of supervision. CONCLUSION: LLMs showed promising capabilities in supporting rehabilitation treatment planning, possibly offering adaptability and personalization. Nonetheless, high-quality studies are necessary to validate real-world effectiveness and define implementation strategies.

items.title: The role of social media and generative-ai in self-directed learning among respiratory therapy interns: a qualitative study
items.abstract: Social media and generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) are increasingly integrated into healthcare education and have the potential to enhance self-directed learning (SDL). Although these technologies are widely used by healthcare students, little is known about how respiratory therapy interns use social media and GenAI to support their SDL during clinical training. This qualitative study adopted an interpretivist approach to explore respiratory therapy interns’ experiences of using social media and generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) to support self-directed learning (SDL). A total population sampling strategy was employed, whereby all 25 eligible respiratory therapy interns undertaking their internship at one Saudi hospital were invited to participate. Nineteen interns consented to participate and completed semi-structured interviews. Data were analyzed using Braun and Clarke’s thematic analysis. Four themes were identified. First, participants conceptualized SDL as an independent learning process in which they assumed responsibility for identifying learning needs and seeking knowledge using digital resources. Second, social media supported SDL by providing accessible educational content, facilitating peer learning and collaboration, identifying learning needs, and supporting examination preparation. Third, GenAI functioned as a personalized learning assistant by simplifying complex concepts, summarizing learning materials and generating practice questions. Finally, participants stressed the importance of responsible use of digital technologies by critically evaluating information, verifying content using trusted sources and recognizing challenges including misinformation, distraction, plagiarism concerns and overreliance on GenAI. Respiratory therapy interns have integrated social media and GenAI into their self-directed learning in both academic and clinical contexts. These technologies complement rather than replace traditional learning resources and may enhance learner autonomy when used critically and responsibly. Healthcare education programs should enable students to develop AI literacy and self-directed learning skills to optimize the educational benefits of emerging technologies while promoting effective use.

items.title: The Trillion-Dollar Illusion?
items.abstract: Summary The industrial system under construction around artificial intelligence is larger, more interconnected and more financially demanding than the familiar image of a software startup suggests. Anthropic filed its U.S. IPO registration statement in October, revealing explosive revenue growth and a layered program of future computing commitments valued in the hundreds of billions. These are genuine developments. The dispute is whether future customer spending will justify the scale, timing and rigidity of the obligations being created today. [1][2][7] An unusual financial pattern connects the major participants: cloud companies invest in laboratories that purchase their services; hardware manufacturers sell the processors and participate in financing demand; infrastructure operators borrow against long-duration customer contracts; alternative asset managers purchase data centers and lease them to technology tenants. The IMF now describes circular financing as a risk transmission mechanism rather than an anecdotal peculiarity. None of this proves fictitious demand. It does mean that investors should not mistake every signed contract, funded data center and equipment sale for independent confirmation of final-customer willingness to pay. [4][14][15][24] The immediate economic contradiction concerns time. AI capabilities are becoming rapidly cheaper: Stanford documented a more than 280-fold decline in the price of GPT-3.5-level inference in approximately eighteen months; the OECD reported nearly an 80% decline in its quality-adjusted model price index through April 2026. Meanwhile the industry is signing leases and computing commitments extending across much of the next decade. If the cost per useful task declines faster than revenues grow, utilization, margins and debt service become decisive. Increasing token usage is not itself proof of increasing profits. [22][23] The physical expansion is real. The IEA estimates data-center electricity demand at 485 TWh in 2025, with a central projection of 950 TWh by 2030. Equipment manufacturing, grids, permits, water and financing do not move at model-release speed. Project Jupiter in New Mexico demonstrates that power and construction delays can interfere with a sophisticated contract chain before the computing it promises has been delivered. A failed project can impose costs beyond its developer if grid upgrades or other public commitments were financed in anticipation of its demand. [17][19][21] The inquiry finds a legitimate commercial market, extraordinary growth and serious structural vulnerabilities. It finds no basis for claiming that laboratory sales are broadly fabricated or that a coordinated financial fraud has been proved. The strongest conclusion is less sensational and more important: AI may create enormous economic value even if some leading model developers, lenders or infrastructure operators fail to capture it. Technological success and the financial survival of particular firms are separate propositions.

items.title: The Website as Brand Source of Truth: Grounding AI-Generated Marketing Content in What a Company Already Says
items.abstract: Generative AI can write scripts, captions and scenes for a company in seconds, but when it is prompted from scratch it fills gaps with plausible inventions and drifts away from what the company actually says about itself. This paper argues that a company's own website is the natural source of truth for AI-generated marketing, provided it is turned into a structured brand record that a person reviews before use. We review evidence that brand equity rests on coherent brand knowledge and that a brand's website shapes how the brand is perceived; that language models hallucinate for documented reasons and drift from their instructions over a conversation; and that grounding generation in retrieved sources reduces hallucination without removing it. Models also tend to follow the context they are given, even when it is wrong, and web content can be outdated or carry injected instructions. From this evidence we derive six design principles, among them reading what the company already publishes, keeping human edits authoritative over automatic re-reads, separating what was read from what was invented, and treating web content as data rather than instructions. We illustrate the principles with GetReelCom, which drafts a reviewable brand record from a company's website, described from its public documentation, and we propose an evaluation. Competing interests: the author is a co-founder of GetReelCom, the application used as the illustrative case. About the author: Amber Kesselaer is a growth consultant and an expert in marketing and AI video generation.

items.title: Theory-Guided Human-AI Collaboration: Focusing, Feedback and Critical Examination in Jean-Pol Martin's Semantic Field
items.abstract: This methodological article examines how Jean-Pol Martin organizes theory-guided collaboration with artificial intelligence through two complementary documents: a theory prompt and a master prompt. The theory prompt supplies the conceptual framework of Learning by Teaching (LdL), the New Human Rights (NMR), and Martin’s semantic field. The master prompt specifies analytical procedures, working expectations, and criteria for provisional claims. Ongoing human feedback connects these instructions to the concrete task. The article’s contribution lies in making the relationship between conceptual grounding, procedural direction, and situated correction explicit. Two episodes from the dialogue leading to this publication illustrate how editorial feedback and the introduction of foundational documents reshape an AI-generated text. Within the developing series on LdL, NMR, and human-AI collaboration, the article functions as a methodological bridge between theoretical exposition and practical application. It offers a reusable procedure for documenting instructions, corrections, and revisions, together with suggestions for comparative evaluation. The organismic reference point of the NMR framework places the living, thinking, social, and meaning-oriented human being at the centre of analysis. Six equal-ranking needs provide its anthropological and normative orientation: thinking, health, security, social belonging, self-realization and participation, and meaning. This is a methodological account with illustrative dialogue episodes, not a controlled study. It distinguishes conceptual coherence from factual validation and practical effectiveness. The article was developed through collaboration between Jean-Pol Martin and ChatGPT. Supplementary materials: The deposit includes the original German master prompt and theory prompt with its organismic supplement. The main article is in English; the supplementary documents are in German.

items.title: tModBase v2.0: an expanded database of tRNA modifications with an AI-powered assistant
items.abstract: Chemical modifications of transfer RNAs (tRNAs) are crucial for tRNA stability, codon decoding, translational fidelity, and tRNA-derived small RNA (tsRNA) biogenesis. Changes in these modifications are associated with stress responses, physiological regulation, and human disease, underscoring the need to integrate modification information with experimental evidence and biological context. We previously established tModBase, a web resource to organize and explore tRNA modification-related data. Its first release integrated modification sites, high-throughput sequencing-derived signals, and condition-dependent changes. Since then, tRNA profiling has expanded through modification-specific and direct RNA sequencing strategies, with rapidly growing datasets across species and conditions. Here, we present tModBase v2.0 (http://www.tmodbase2.com/), containing 528 datasets across 23 species, 40 sequencing and library-preparation methods, and 42 modification types. It includes 68 third-generation and 210 modification-specific sequencing datasets, extending coverage of direct-RNA and modification-specific approaches. tModBase v2.0 further integrates sequencing-derived signals, condition-dependent information, and biological annotations linking modifications with enzymes, genetic variants, tsRNAs, diseases, and expression profiles. The LLM- and retrieval-augmented generation-powered assistant tModBot enables natural-language exploration across database modules while grounding responses in retrieved tModBase evidence. tModBase v2.0 therefore provides an expanded resource for investigating the diversity, dynamics, and biological context of tRNA modifications.

items.title: Transforming Industries Through AI: Strategic Management Approaches and Intersectoral Synergies
items.abstract: The development of the artificial intelligence preconditions changes in the methods of management in the sectors, new opportunities of innovation and strategic cooperation. AI has now been a defining factor of productivity, judgment, and competitive edge in many industries-both health care and banking and manufacturing and retail and notably in education. The purpose of this essay is to track the way in which AI is going to revolutionize the traditional practices through assimilation with management activities in marketing, operations, strategic planning, and human resources. AI-driven analytics will ensure one is swift to the emerging market circumstances because it can enhance decision-making through information-driven understanding, predictive modeling as well as real-time prediction. The AI in operations streamlines the supply chain management, automates manufacturing processes at low costs, and does not affect quality. The marketing strategies whereby AI tools can foresee consumer behavior, enhance the campaign, and provide customer experiences that make them more loyal to the brand. AI also simplifies performance monitoring, training, and hiring in HR, freeing the manager to work on other vital projects. On the promise of change, the very basic concerns are of data security and integrity, ethics, and retraining of the workforce. This study would thus advocate for the strategic need to use the AI capability toward business objectives for long-term growth. Finally, there have to be synergies that enable productivity, creativity, and values between human knowledge and machine intelligence. This is very crucial in the management system that will prevail during the AI age. It is impressive how the AI can disrupt and facilitate strategic management using case studies and company practices. What is inferred here is that those companies that succeed in harnessing the promise and addressing the obstacles of AI will form the prototype for driving influence in future dynamics of the industry and global competitiveness. In other words, AI is a management paradigm shift with the easy facilitation of being flexible, teamwork, and creativity, with technical growth.

items.title: TRANSHUMANISM IN THE AGE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE:THE SOCIO-PHILOSOPHICAL DIMENSIONS OF THE DIGITAL SOCIETY
items.abstract: The relevance of the study. The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence, biotechnology, and neural interfaces underscores the need for a socio-philosophical analysis of transhumanism as a philosophical movement that advocates the possibility and desirability of technologically enhancing human nature. As digital society takes shape, transhumanist ideas are moving beyond academic discourse to become a driving force behind real-world social transformations, raising fundamentally new questions about the nature of human agency, the boundaries between the natural and the artificial, and the future social order. This article aims to examine the socio-philosophical dimensions of transhumanism in the age of artificial intelligence through an analysis of the movement’s key conceptual foundations, its interconnection with the processes of digitalisation, and a critical reflection on the associated risks and prospects. The study’s methodological framework is based on its stated aim and research objectives and adopts an interdisciplinary approach drawing on social philosophy, technology ethics, the social sciences, and media studies. The study employs comparative- historical analysis, the phenomenological method, critical discourse analysis, and a systems approach to investigating the social consequences of technological development. Research findings. The intellectual origins of transhumanism have been traced, from FM-2030’s futurist manifestos to contemporary concepts of the technological singularity and superintelligence. The analysis shows that digital society creates a distinct socio-technical environment in which transhumanist transformations assume concrete forms and give rise to new social tensions. Three key tensions within the transhumanist project have been identified: between individual freedom of self-improvement and its systemic social consequences; between techno-optimistic predictions and the real risks of humanity losing control over powerful technological systems; and between the pursuit of boundless self-improvement and the threat posed by the erosion of essential human qualities as the foundation of moral and legal equality. It is emphasised that a socio-philosophical understanding of transhumanism requires moving beyond the binary opposition between techno-optimism and technophobia in favour of a balanced, critical, and humanistically oriented approach that combines recognition of the genuine possibilities of technological progress with responsible consideration of its limits and risks.

items.abstract: Chapter 2 examines the potential of the semiconductor technology applied to integrated circuits in the form of chips. The benefits of shrinking the dimensions of integrated circuits are explained. Illustrations to help readers realize the micrometer and nanometer dimensions are given. Optical lithography, a critical technology enabling shrinking integrated circuits from the minimum feature size in the order of 7.5 micrometers to 2 nanometers, is explained in simple terms using schematic figures to show the exposure equipment, patterns on mask and on wafer, the exposure, development, and etch patterning processes. Key equations on optical scaling and electric scaling laws are introduced. To impress the readers with the potential of semiconductor technology and integrated circuits, their applications to human activities are given. They include consumer electronics, such as smartphones, televisions, immersive audio, cleaning robots, washing machines, refrigerators, microwave ovens, air conditioners, thermostats, security cameras, etc. Automobiles nowadays also need chips to control the engine, assist the driver for manual or automated driving, infotainment systems, battery management, etc. Then, there are medical devices, industrial applications, telecommunication, aerospace and defense, computing and data processing, audio and signal processing, and artificial intelligence. The chapter closes with the direction of technology development, post-scaling.

items.title: Trust in artificial intelligence and AI-assisted social and civic decision-making among Arab youth: evidence from Egypt, Kuwait, and the UAE
items.abstract: Introduction Trust in artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly shapes how young people evaluate information and public issues, yet evidence from Arab contexts remains limited. This study examined the socio-technical correlates of trust in AI and its association with AI-assisted social and civic decision-making among digitally engaged youth in Egypt, Kuwait, and the United Arab Emirates. Methods A cross-sectional online survey was conducted with 1,023 respondents aged 18–35 recruited through purposive, non-probability sampling. Confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), structural equation modeling (SEM), multi-group CFA, and competing full- versus partial-mediation models evaluated measurement and structural relationships. Results The partially mediated model fit significantly better than the fully mediated model, Δχ2(5) = 55.66, p < 0.001. Institutional confidence (β = 0.303), AI literacy (β = 0.281), perceived usefulness (β = 0.242), and social influence (β = 0.107) were positively associated with trust in AI, and perceived risk was negatively associated (β = −0.106; all p < 0.001). Trust was positively associated with AI-assisted decision-making (β = 0.412, p < 0.001). Significant indirect associations through trust were observed for all five antecedents, while the direct perceived-risk path to AI-assisted decision-making was nonsignificant. Multi-group CFA supported metric and practical scalar measurement invariance across the three countries. Discussion The findings support a socio-technical account of AI trust in which technological, cognitive, institutional, and social conditions jointly relate to AI-assisted decision-making, with trust functioning as a central but not exclusive pathway. Given the cross-sectional, purposive design, findings are interpreted as associations rather than causal or nationally representative effects.

items.title: Trustworthy Federated Clinical Intelligence with Homomorphic Encryption and Explainable AI
items.abstract: Cross-institutional clinical artificial intelligence is constrained by fragmented patient data, non-identically distributed (non-IID) populations, leakage from shared model updates, and limited interpretability. Federated learning (FL) preserves data locality, but ordinary FL neither makes model updates confidential nor guarantees stable optimization under heterogeneous clients. This paper proposes a defense-in-depth framework that coordinates Federated Proximal (FedProx) optimization, record-level differential privacy (DP), Cheon–Kim–Kim–Song (CKKS) approximate homomorphic encryption, and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI). FedProx limits local model drift; DP-SGD bounds the influence of an individual training record; and CKKS permits weighted aggregation while client updates remain encrypted. A key-separated design keeps the aggregation server from being provisioned with the secret key used to reveal individual contributions; only the aggregate is released for global-model construction. Grad-CAM and SHAP/LIME provide clinician-facing explanations, while an audit dashboard reports convergence, privacy-accounting inputs, encryption status, and systems overhead. We formalize the learning objective, privacy mechanism, encrypted aggregation, threat model, numerical approximation error, communication footprint, and an evaluation protocol spanning IID and controlled non-IID partitions. The contribution is a reproducible system-level co-design and evaluation framework rather than a new cryptographic primitive or optimization algorithm.

items.title: Truthful, Wise, and Responsible
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly entering dental education, and recent reviews report both its benefits and recurring concerns about factual inaccuracy, academic integrity, over-reliance, bias, and privacy. Existing responses are largely technical and regulatory; they specify what should be done but say little about the character of the educators and students who use AI. This critical integrative review proposes a Christian virtue framework, grounded in the doctrine of the imago Dei, to guide dental educators and students. Empirical literature on AI in dental and health-professions education was read alongside Catholic and evangelical documents on AI and Christian scholarship on education and personhood. Five virtues, identified from Christian virtue-ethics literature on AI, were mapped to the main AI issues: truthfulness (hallucinated content and academic integrity), practical wisdom (automation bias, overconfidence, and deskilling), responsibility (accountability for AI-supported decisions), justice (bias and unequal access), and love (empathy, the clinician–patient relationship, and privacy). For each virtue, implications for educators and students are outlined. The framework suggests that responsible AI use in dental education is a matter not only of policy but also of formation, and it offers Christian dental schools a basis for curricula and institutional guidance.

items.title: Understanding Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: This chapter provides a foundational understanding of AI by examining its relationship to human intelligence, its historical evolution, core technologies, and practical applications. It begins by exploring the concepts of cognitive, emotional, and social intelligence and demonstrates how AI primarily emulates aspects of human cognitive reasoning. This chapter introduces the major subsets of AI, including Machine Learning, Deep Learning, Natural Language Processing (NPL), Computer Vision, Expert Systems, and Robotics, while distinguishing AI models from AI systems and explaining their roles in modern decision-making. It also examines AI data requirements, the AI life cycle, and the importance of high-quality data, model training, evaluation, deployment, and continual improvement. Recognizing that AI is not inherently accurate or unbiased, this chapter emphasizes the need for effective governance, ethical principles, transparency, and human oversight. Finally, it introduces the distinction between enterprise-level AI governance and the micro-level governance of AI applications within an ESH Management System, providing the conceptual foundation for the responsible integration of AI throughout the remainder of the book.

items.title: Uneven automation: comparing authorship anxiety and generative AI use among art and design undergraduate students
items.abstract: Art and design education expects students to develop a sense of authorship over original work, but generative AI (GenAI) complicates how students understand and claim that authorship. This study examined whether these experiences differ across creative fields through a mixed-methods design. The survey included 2,441 GenAI-using students from seven field categories at 33 art and design institutions in China and assessed authorship anxiety, creative agency, perceived usefulness, dependence on GenAI, and frequency of use. The quantitative analysis first examined variation across all seven categories and then compared fine art with the five applied design fields. Interview data from 22 survey participants were also examined thematically. The main findings include that (1) authorship anxiety did not differ significantly across the seven categories or between fine art and pooled design; the latter comparison met the equivalence criterion at ±d = 0.20, but not at tighter bounds; (2) clearer differences emerged in how students used GenAI. Compared with fine-art students, design students considered GenAI more useful and used it more frequently; (3) across the interviews, most students described authorship as retaining control over the creative idea while delegating parts of its execution to GenAI. Specifically, fine-art students often grounded authorship in embodied making and human imperfection, whereas design students placed greater emphasis on judgement, selection, and control. We call this pattern uneven automation: concern about authorship was broadly shared, but students in different fields responded to GenAI in different ways, potentially reflecting the varying labour-market pressures surrounding their disciplines.

items.title: Use of Large Language Models for Automated Short-Answer Question Grading in Second-Cycle Medical Education: Performance and Consistency Evaluation Study
items.abstract: BACKGROUND Short-answer questions (SAQs) effectively assess higher-order reasoning skills in medical education but face challenges in scalability due to time-intensive manual grading and concerns about interrater reliability. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) may offer a solution through automated assessment. OBJECTIVE This study evaluated the performance and consistency of LLMs—ChatGPT, Claude Sonnet 4, and Mistral Pro—compared with those of human graders for SAQ grading in hepatology and gastroenterology. METHODS We retrospectively analyzed SAQs from hepatology and gastroenterology examinations at Sorbonne University, Paris, France (2023-2025). Three human evaluators (2 hepatogastroenterologists and 1 radiologist) independently graded all responses twice, with the majority consensus score serving as the reference standard. Six LLMs were evaluated: ChatGPT (GPT-4o, GPT-4.5, GPT-4o3, and GPT-5), Claude Sonnet 4, and Mistral Pro. Each LLM graded all responses twice using standardized prompts, including questions, model answers, grading guidelines, and scoring rubrics. Agreement was assessed using quadratic weighted kappa (QWK), Cohen κ, the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), and the mean absolute error (MAE) for interhuman, intrahuman, LLM-versus-human, and intramodel comparisons. RESULTS A total of 902 student responses from 12 SAQs were included and analyzed. Interhuman grader agreement was almost perfect (QWK 0.90-0.92; ICC 0.90-0.92; MAE 0.05-0.07). Claude Sonnet 4 and GPT-4o3 demonstrated near-human–level performance when compared with the majority vote of human evaluators (Claude Sonnet 4: QWK 0.88-0.90; ICC 0.88-0.90; MAE 0.06-0.07 and GPT-4o3: QWK 0.82-0.89; ICC 0.82-0.89; MAE 0.07-0.09). GPT-5 showed substantial agreement (QWK 0.77-0.79). Mistral Pro and older ChatGPT versions performed poorly (QWK <0.63). Intramodel consistency was the highest for Claude Sonnet 4 (QWK 0.93), approaching the best human intrarater reliability. Agreement did not correlate with prompt design choices (number of examples or minimum word count). CONCLUSIONS Advanced LLMs, particularly Claude Sonnet 4 and GPT-4o3, demonstrated near-human–level grading performance, supporting their potential use as assistive tools in SAQ grading. However, performance varied by model, and agreement alone does not ensure educational validity. Until broader multicenter validation is conducted across diverse domains, stakes, and question formats—along with safeguards for bias, privacy, and model drift—LLMs should augment rather than replace human faculty graders.

items.title: Utilising wearable technology to enhance neurosurgical training: a systematic scoping review
items.abstract: PURPOSE: Contemporary neurosurgical training faces challenges due to reduced operative exposure and the limited, inconsistent feedback provided to trainees. Wearable technologies may help address these issues by offering objective data and real-time support. This scoping review systematically evaluates the evidence of wearable technology in surgical training, analysing device types, their applications, and the supporting evidence for their effectiveness. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A systematic literature search was conducted in 10 pre-clinical and clinical databases from inception to May 2024, searching for keywords "wearable technology" AND "surgery" AND "training". The search yielded 25,806 results. After removing duplicates, papers were screened by title and abstract (n = 12,306), followed by full-text screening (n = 482). RESULTS: Forty-one studies, including 985 participants, were included in the review. Head-mounted displays were predominantly used for augmented and mixed reality applications, while smart glasses facilitated telementoring and procedure recording. Other wearables enabled biomechanical analysis and ergonomic assessments. Reported outcomes varied widely, with clinician-centred metrics, such as procedural accuracy, error rates, completion times, and satisfaction, being the most frequently assessed. Devices including HTC VIVE and HoloLens were associated with improved surgical performance. Clinicians often reported enhanced visualisation and anatomical orientation, though barriers such as learning curves, technical issues, and discomfort were noted. CONCLUSIONS: This review provides a comprehensive evaluation of wearable technologies in surgical training, highlighting their potential to improve performance metrics and support a range of educational uses for neurosurgical trainees. However, key challenges must be addressed to enable broader adoption and integration into surgical education.

items.title: Verified-Sender: Improving Safe Message Detection in SMiShing
items.abstract: SMS phishing poses a significant threat. Small mobile displays lack the sender’s address transparency. A signal nudge in the representation of a checkmark shield icon is proposed as a verified-sender cue to aid in the identification of safe messages. This experiment examines whether the presence of this nudge impacts users’ ability to distinguish between safe and malicious messages. Our findings suggest that the nudge significantly improved the accuracy of safe message detection by 10%, while the accuracy of malicious message detection remained unchanged. The nudge serves as a positive verified-sender cue that helps users confirm safe messages, but, on its own, does not help users reject phishing. Additionally, no detectable increase in perceived workload (NASA-TLX) was found. The implemented nudge does not function as a phishing defense. Instead, it helps users recognize legitimate messages as safe without any spillover resistance to malicious messages.

items.title: Visualizing use of generative artificial intelligence in higher education
items.abstract: Purpose Higher education students are engaged with academic learning and research using generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) applications. A major shift in pedagogical approach surfaces many challenges to academic integrity that urging to redefining assessment model and ethical literacy. This study aims to investigate impact of the GenAI apps among the students using survey of technical and non-technical disciplines. Survey is mainly focused on: use of GenAI apps, variations in observed effectiveness and student’s usage pattern, level of adoption and acceptance of GenAI apps. Reviews of existing literature on the implications of GenAI and emerging need for systemic changes are discussed with reference to result. Design/methodology/approach Survey was developed to assess the integration of GenAI apps in the higher education. It was conducted with undergraduate and postgraduate students so as to find the adoption and acceptance rate of GenAI apps among the students; it has been partitioned into two categories: non-technical disciplines and technical disciplines. Students from the social science and pure sciences are in the non-technical disciplines, while students from computer science and engineering students are in the technical discipline. The questionnaire included a mix of multiple-choice questions, scale items and open-ended responses. Findings This research is classified for students into technical and non-technical disciplines, revealing notable differences in adoption patterns. First, students from non-technical disciplines are not entirely using GenAI applications. Second, effectiveness of the usage can be analyzed by the purpose of usage of GenAI apps which is shown by graphs. However, technical students show higher inclination for AI usages. Third, regarding adoption or acceptance, many rural students initially adopt it through classmates or roommates. In contrast, students in urban areas, especially in technical disciplines, spend higher hours; here, they accept the technology and update themselves with new technology. Research limitations/implications The survey did not assess the accuracy or effectiveness of GenAI outputs. This is a limitation for drawing conclusions about the performance quality of these apps across disciplines. Originality/value Students come from different parts of India, so it is also possible that the places where they previously studied lacked facilities such as internet connectivity and stable power supply. This influences the usage. Students from many disciplines participated in the survey, so their perspective to look at the GenAI apps is a unique feature. GenAI apps are accepted among technical students, and non-technical students are gradually adopting. Over-reliance may hinder the individual learning and creativity; it can be an aid to the learning but not as a supplement of human intelligence. Universities face challenges in formulating policies.

items.title: Where Do We Look? Visual Attention Competition Between Hyper-Salient Objects and AI-Generated Virtual Endorsers in Generative Artificial Intelligence Advertising
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) advertising, defined as advertising content created or substantially assisted by generative AI systems (AIGC), has introduced new visual features that combine algorithmically generated objects with human-like representations. Hyper-salient objects, defined by exaggerated perceptual prominence and semantic incongruity, and AI-generated virtual endorsers, represented by human-like AI-created figures, have become increasingly common in such advertisements. However, little is known about how these distinct visual cues compete for consumers’ limited attentional resources when presented together. Drawing on visual attention and scene perception perspectives, this study investigated how hyper-salient objects and AI-generated virtual endorsers influence visual attention allocation in AI-generated advertising. A 2 (hyper-salient object: present vs. absent) × 2 (AI endorser: present vs. absent) between-subjects eye-tracking experiment was conducted with 160 participants in a controlled laboratory setting using static AI-generated advertisements. Eye movements were recorded, and memory was assessed using signal detection measures (d′) from a recognition task involving target and distractor advertisements. Advertising attitude and product trust were measured using established scales. Results from linear and generalized linear mixed-effects models showed that hyper-salient objects increased early fixation probability and attracted a larger dwell time proportion, demonstrating strong attentional capture. AI-generated endorsers also attracted attention when presented alone, but their proportional attention share decreased when hyper-salient objects were simultaneously present. The effects of these visual elements on memory and product trust were conditional on their co-occurrence rather than uniform across conditions. Within the specific set of experimentally constructed stimuli and four sampled product categories, this research contributes to AIGC advertising literature by developing a visual competition perspective on how multiple AI-generated visual cues interact under limited attentional capacity, offering implications for designing effective generative AI advertisements.

items.title: Whose Judgement Counts? An Appraisal-Informed Critical Discourse Analysis of Educational AI Communications
items.abstract: Public guidance on generative AI asks students to exercise judgement while institutions and platforms define the conditions of use. This study examines how these texts distribute authority over writing, evidence and assessment. The purposively selected corpus comprises eight official webpages from three UK universities and Google and captions from three educational videos, retrieved in October 2026. Appraisal-informed critical discourse analysis examines 30 decision-focused units: passages addressing a particular choice or responsibility. Analysis also considers modality and legitimation, meaning the reasons offered to justify a practice. The main finding is boundary maintenance: texts distinguish what fluent writing, technical capability or disclosure can establish about learning, reliability and permission. University guidance and Gemini promotion both value learner participation, although they serve different purposes. Staff guidance also encourages discussion of assessment criteria. These findings suggest that teachers should explain acceptable assistance, student responsibilities and opportunities to question criteria. The small documentary corpus supports interpretation of published communications, not conclusions about classroom practice or AI effectiveness.

items.abstract: This paper examines why cryptocurrency exchanges remain vulnerable to cyberattacks by comparing two security incidents: Bybit in February 2025 and Binance in October 2026. Using statements from the companies involved, news reports, and data from 220 cryptocurrency exchange incidents between 2009 and 2024, the study explores common vulnerabilities, attack methods, financial impacts, and potential solutions.The findings identify recurring vulnerabilities, including wallet and key compromises, unauthorized access, human error, and third-party services. The paper also discusses emerging risks associated with quantum computing and AI agents with financial capabilities. In addition, it presents security recommendations such as improved key management, secure transaction processes, stronger employee and third-party security, and better recovery plans.The Binance incident is still under investigation; therefore, some reported figures and findings may change.

items.title: Why Do University Students Use AI: Drivers and Barriers?
items.abstract: As generative artificial intelligence becomes integrated into academic life, understanding what drives student adoption is essential for informed institutional policy. This study examines AI engagement among 672 students at a public midsize southern university, integrating the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and Social Cognitive Theory (SCT) to evaluate eight constructs: perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, perceived trust, perceived risk, social influence, self-efficacy, anxiousness, and affection. Survey data show students frequently use AI for information retrieval and writing assistance, while specialized applications such as graphic and video generation remain underutilized. Regression analysis shows perceived usefulness, affection, and trust are the primary positive predictors of adoption, whereas anxiety and perceived risk are significant deterrents. Notably, affection, the emotional enjoyment of technology, emerged as one of the most consistent motivators across academic tasks, from research to creative ideation. These results suggest emotional and trust-based factors are as critical as functional utility in shaping student behavior. Universities should prioritize emotional comfort and ethical trust alongside technical training to foster responsible, confident AI integration..

items.title: Why so serious? Generative AI in Knowledge-Work from a Text-Workers’ Perspective
items.abstract: Generative AI (genAI) systems have become an integral part of scientific text-producing practice. They can conduct literature-related research, organize content and information, proofread text, and assist with writing itself. Above all, they are credited with reducing workload by taking on or taking over these routine tasks. Drawing on an internal, interdisciplinary KIT-ITAS project that deployed the genAI-supported research assistance system 'Undermind.ai', we demonstrate that the potential to reduce workload is offset by the need to reorganize basic scientific competencies in response to the changing workflow requirements of genAI-assisted knowledge work. GenAI systems produce texts that closely resemble stylistic conventions and appear both well-formed and plausible. However, the closer these texts adhere to researchers’ expectations, the more challenging it becomes to verify their content using established academic methods. This generates higher-order efforts that must be weighed against existing working standards for assessing text-based results. The constant validation and ongoing negotiation of plausibility with the system’s output, both during and beyond the writing process, places additional demands on researchers’ critical competence and judgement. Using genAI in knowledge work thus shifts the focus of familiar textual and intellectual labour practices and procedures away from independent creation and toward the verification of textual output, along with the corresponding demands on epistemic attention, responsibility, authorization, and authority.

items.title: Writing and Amending the Clinical Protocol: IND and CTA Lifecycle Strategy for Targeted RAS Pathway Inhibitors in Advanced Solid Tumors
items.abstract: Targeted inhibitors of the RAS signaling pathway have moved from a historically undruggable target class to a growing portfolio of clinically active agents in advanced solid tumors, including pancreatic, colorectal, and non-small cell lung cancer. This article is written from the perspective of a clinical trial manager responsible for carrying a RAS pathway inhibitor program from its initial Investigational New Drug (IND) application or Clinical Trial Application (CTA) through the protocol amendments that inevitably follow as early clinical data accumulate. It reviews the mechanistic rationale for this drug class, the rationale for trial phase, setting, and population selection, best practices for first-in-human and dose-expansion protocol design, anticipated risks and pharmacovigilance monitoring strategy, statistical sample-size rationale drawn from registered trials, the detailed regulatory requirements, templates, and timelines governing both the initial IND or CTA submission and subsequent amendments under FDA, Health Canada, and EMA frameworks, a representative schedule of assessments spanning a twelve-month treatment period, and the application of artificial intelligence tools to data capture and data quality. The article closes with recommendations for regulatory affairs and clinical operations professionals managing this therapeutic category.Keywords: RAS pathway inhibitors; KRAS; protocol amendment; Investigational New Drug application; Clinical Trial Application; pharmacovigilance; sample size; regulatory artificial intelligence

items.title: ЯВИЩЕ КОНЦЕНТРАЦІЙНОЇ ПОЛЯРИЗАЦІЇ: СТАН ПРОБЛЕМИІ АКТУАЛЬНІ НАПРЯМКИ ДОСЛІДЖЕНЬ
items.abstract: Concentration polarization is one of the key mass transfer phenomena occurring in membrane separation processes, electrochemical systems, heat and mass transfer equipment, and numerous technological processes in power engineering and industrial machinery. The phenomenon is associated with the formation of a concentration boundary layer near the phase interface, where the concentration of dissolved substances differs significantly from that in the bulk solution. This results in additional diffusion resistance, reduced process productivity, increased energy consumption, accelerated membrane fouling, and shortened equipment service life. As the requirements for energy efficiency, operational reliability, and environmental sustainability continue to increase, concentration polarization has become one of the major challenges limiting the performance of modern membrane and mass transfer systems. The aim of this study is to summarize the current state of research on concentration polarization in membrane-based water treatment and desalination processes, to analyze the physical mechanisms responsible for its formation, to review contemporary theoretical, numerical, and experimental approaches to its investigation, and to identify promising directions for minimizing its adverse effects. The study is based on a comprehensive analysis and systematization of recent scientific publications devoted to reverse osmosis, nanofiltration, ultrafiltration, microfiltration, and forward osmosis technologies. Particular attention is given to modern mathematical models describing concentration polarization, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations, and advanced experimental techniques, including digital holographic interferometry and laser-induced fluorescence, which enable direct visualization of concentration boundary layers and local mass transfer phenomena. The influence of membrane structure, channel geometry, hydrodynamic conditions, flow turbulators, and membrane surface properties on the development of concentration polarization is analyzed. Special consideration is also given to internal concentration polarization in forward osmosis membranes and to recent advances in nanocomposite membrane materials designed to reduce concentration polarization and membrane fouling. The review demonstrates that integrating experimental observations with numerical simulations provides new opportunities for understanding and controlling concentration polarization in complex engineering systems. Furthermore, the rapid development of digital twins, artificial intelligence, and machine learning technologies creates new possibilities for predictive modeling, process optimization, and intelligent control of membrane systems. The practical significance of the study lies in the systematization of modern approaches aimed at mitigating concentration polarization and membrane fouling, the results of which can be applied in the design, optimization, and operation of membrane equipment for water treatment, desalination, and other industrial mass transfer processes.

items.abstract: Исследование основано на практическом вопросе, с которым всё чаще сталкиваются органы государственного планирования в Центральной Азии: насколько надёжны линейные модели при оценке влияния цифровизации, искусственного интеллекта и факторов устойчивого развития и достаточна ли их предсказательная способность для описания реальных социально-экономических процессов? Для ответа на данный вопрос была сформирована сбалансированная панель данных по 34 развивающимся экономикам и экономикам переходного типа за 2012–2024 гг., включая пять стран Центральной Азии: Узбекистан, Казахстан, Кыргызстан, Таджикистан и Туркменистан. В исследовании использованы открытые базы данных Всемирного банка (World Development Indicators), Международного союза электросвязи (ICT Development Index), Всемирной организации интеллектуальной собственности (Global Innovation Index), а также рейтинги ESG Country Risk. На одном и том же массиве данных были построены две группы моделей. Первая основана на классической эконометрике панельных данных и включает сквозную регрессию методом наименьших квадратов (МНК), модель с фиксированными эффектами и модель со случайными эффектами. Вторая объединяет четыре алгоритма машинного обучения: Ridge и Lasso как регуляризованные линейные модели, а также Random Forest и Gradient Boosting как ансамблевые методы на основе деревьев решений. Качество моделей сравнивалось на отложенной 20%-ной тестовой выборке по трём метрикам: коэффициенту детерминации (R²), среднеквадратичной ошибке и средней абсолютной ошибке. Полученные результаты свидетельствуют о существенном преимуществе модели Gradient Boosting. Она объяснила 96,8% дисперсии ESG-индекса против 81,2% у обычной линейной регрессии, при этом ошибка прогноза сократилась более чем в два раза — с 5,18 до 2,14 пункта. Данное преимущество связано не только с подбором коэффициентов, но и с различиями в природе рассматриваемых моделей: алгоритмы на основе деревьев решений способны выявлять пороговые эффекты и взаимодействия между переменными, которые в линейной спецификации усредняются в рамках единой функциональной зависимости. Расчёт важности признаков показал, что готовность к использованию искусственного интеллекта и уровень цифровизации совместно формируют более половины объясняющей способности модели, опережая по значимости даже ВВП на душу населения. Отдельный раздел статьи посвящён Узбекистану, индекс цифровизации которого за тринадцать лет увеличился почти втрое. На основе полученных результатов сформулированы три практические рекомендации по совершенствованию национальной системы ESG-мониторинга. EN The study is based on a practical question that public planning authorities in Central Asia are increasingly facing: how reliable are linear models in assessing the impact of digitalization, artificial intelligence, and sustainable development factors, and is their predictive capacity sufficient to describe real socio-economic processes? To address this question, a balanced panel dataset covering 34 developing and transition economies for the period 2012–2024 was constructed, including five Central Asian countries: Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Turkmenistan. The study uses open data from the World Bank (World Development Indicators), the International Telecommunication Union (ICT Development Index), the World Intellectual Property Organization (Global Innovation Index), as well as ESG Country Risk ratings. Two groups of models were developed using the same dataset. The first is based on classical panel-data econometrics and includes pooled ordinary least squares (OLS) regression, a fixed-effects model, and a random-effects model. The second group combines four machine-learning algorithms: Ridge and Lasso as regularized linear models, as well as Random Forest and Gradient Boosting as ensemble methods based on decision trees. Model performance was compared on a 20% holdout test sample using three metrics: the coefficient of determination (R²), root mean squared error, and mean absolute error. The results demonstrate a substantial advantage of the Gradient Boosting model. It explained 96.8% of the variance in the ESG index compared with 81.2% for conventional linear regression, while the prediction error decreased by more than half, from 5.18 to 2.14 points. This advantage is associated not only with coefficient estimation but also with fundamental differences in the nature of the models: decision-tree-based algorithms are capable of identifying threshold effects and interactions among variables that are averaged within a single functional relationship in linear specifications. Feature-importance analysis showed that AI readiness and the level of digitalization jointly account for more than half of the model's explanatory power, exceeding even GDP per capita in importance. A separate section of the article focuses on Uzbekistan, whose digitalization index increased almost threefold over thirteen years. Based on the results obtained, three practical recommendations are formulated for improving the national ESG monitoring system. items.abstract: Abstract This study presents a bibliometric mapping of the academic literature on airport security, aiming to chart the intellectual structure, thematic evolution, and collaboration patterns of the field and to translate these patterns into implications for security practitioners and policymakers. A total of 1,207 documents indexed in the Scopus database between 2010 and March 2025 were retrieved and analyzed using bibliometric mapping techniques implemented in VOSviewer. Co-authorship, keyword co-occurrence, publication-trend, and subject-area analyses were conducted to identify the most influential authors, the dominant research themes, and the disciplinary distribution of the field. The co-authorship network revealed ten major clusters comprising 44 authors and 102 connections, with Adrian Schwaninger emerging as the most central author, reflecting a distinct human-factors research tradition alongside a fast-growing computer-vision tradition. The keyword co-occurrence analysis identified 49 keywords occurring at least six times among 3,062 unique keywords, with “airport security,” “security,” “deep learning,” and “aviation security” as the most frequent terms. Publication output rose markedly after 2019, driven mainly by research on deep learning, X-ray imaging, object detection, and threat-recognition systems. Engineering and computer science were the leading subject areas. Beyond mapping the field, the study translates these findings into concrete implications for airport security operators and regulators, and identifies underexplored themes—including passenger experience, policy design, and the integration of human-factors and automated-detection research—that merit further investigation.

items.title: A Comparative Study of Tokenization Efficiency in English, Hindi, Marathi and Romanized Hinglish Across OpenAI Tokenizer Generations
items.abstract: Large language models read text as small pieces called tokens. The number of tokens decides how much text fits in a model’s context window and how much a token-billed service charges. Recent studies show that Indian languages need many more tokens than English, and that Hinglish, which is Hindi written in English letters, creates its own tokenization problems. However, to our knowledge, Marathi, Hindi and several spellings of Hinglish have not been compared side by side as tokenizers have improved. We built 99 parallel sentences in English, Marathi, Hindi and three Hinglish spellings, and counted their tokens with four OpenAI tokenizer encodings, from older to newer. On the oldest encodings, Marathi and Hindi needed 7.4 and 7.6 times as many tokens as English. On the newest, o200k_base, they needed 1.80 and 1.54 times as many. Hinglish needed 1.8 to 2.2 times as many tokens on the oldest encodings and 1.5 to 1.9 times on the newest, so it was much cheaper than Hindi on older tokenizers but not on the newest. Different Hinglish spellings of the same sentence changed token counts by 26% to 31% on average. These results show that the cost of writing in Indian languages depends strongly on the tokenizer and on the script and spelling a user chooses. The data and code are available at https://github.com/samruddhibelsare-max/hinglsh_tokenization_study.

items.title: A Comparison of the Effectiveness of AI-Assisted Learning versus Conventional Media for Children
items.abstract: This study examined the comparative effectiveness of artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted learning and conventional instructional media among fourth- and fifth-grade elementary school students. Although AI is increasingly promoted as a means of personalizing instruction, empirical evidence directly comparing AI-based and conventional approaches at the elementary level remains limited. A quasi-experimental Pretest-Posttest Control Group Design was employed, involving 42 students in an AI-assisted experimental group and 42 students in a conventionally taught control group drawn from intact classrooms within the same school. Learning effectiveness was operationalized through normalized gain (N-Gain) scores derived from pretest and posttest achievement tests previously established as valid and reliable. Because the experimental group's N-Gain scores departed from a normal distribution, between-group differences were examined using the Mann-Whitney U test, complemented by Cohen's d to estimate practical significance. Results showed that although the two groups began with statistically equivalent pretest scores, the experimental group achieved a significantly higher N-Gain (M = 0.40, medium category) than the control group (M = 0.26, low category), U = 1190.500, p = .006, with a medium effect size (d = 0.551). These findings indicate that AI-assisted learning produced greater and more consistent improvement than conventional media among elementary learners. The study contributes empirical evidence to the underrepresented area of AI-supported elementary education and offers practical guidance for teachers, curriculum developers, and policymakers integrating AI into classroom instruction.

items.title: A Comprehensive Review of ANN-Driven Smart Learning Environments via Brain-Computer Interfacing
items.abstract: The contemporary educational landscape is undergoing a radical transition toward data-intensive, interactive paradigms characterized by the integration of sophisticated artificial intelligence and neurosensing technologies. This review examines the convergence of Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCI) and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) as a transformative force in the creation of "Smart Learning Rooms." By synthesizing current research on Electroencephalography (EEG)-based cognitive monitoring and neural network-driven adaptive systems, this paper delineates a novel conceptual framework for a closed loop pedagogical environment. The study explores the mechanics of real-time attention assessment, the categorization of student learning styles, and the prediction of academic trajectories using diverse ANN architectures, including Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks and multi-layer perceptions. Furthermore, the analysis evaluates the efficacy of neurofeedback in enhancing focus and skill acquisition while addressing the technical, ethical, and socio-economic challenges inherent in the "neuro-digital divide." The proposed framework demonstrates how brain signal monitoring and neural computation can collaborate to personalize instructional pacing, improve engagement, and provide objective performance indicators. The ultimate objective is to provide a rigorous synthesis of the current state of neuro-education and offer a blueprint for the development of fully adaptive, brain-responsive instructional environments.

items.title: A CT Lesion Foundation Model for Non‐Invasive Assessment of Hepatocellular Carcinoma Aggressiveness and Prediction of Recurrence Risk
items.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, with high recurrence rates following curative resection. Accurate non-invasive assessment of tumor aggressiveness and recurrence risk is critical for surgical decision-making and postoperative surveillance, yet remains challenging with conventional imaging modalities. Here, we developed a CT lesion foundation model (LFM), trained via self-supervised learning on 32,120 generic lesion and 6,387 HCC-specific CT patches to capture transferable intra-lesional imaging phenotypes. Across one internal and two external validation cohorts, the sequentially pretrained LFM (LFM-Seq) achieved area under the curve values of 0.916, 0.846, and 0.920 for microvascular invasion (MVI) assessment, and 0.833, 0.885 and 0.795 for pathological grade assessment. The model remained robust under scenarios of limited training data and tumor localization perturbations. Furthermore, LFM-Seq-derived risk scores stratified recurrence-free survival (RFS), yielding an externally validated C-index of 0.701, and remained independently associated with RFS after adjusting for clinicopathological factors. Exploratory biological interpretability analyses showed that LFM-Seq-derived risk phenotypes were associated with suppressed lymphocyte-related immune programs. These results suggest that CT lesion foundation models can support non-invasive and robust characterization of HCC aggressiveness, recurrence risk stratification and discovery of interpretable prognostic imaging biomarkers.

items.title: A Machine Learning Model to Predict Spinal Compression Force During Manual Lifting: Comparison of the Model Performance With Marker-Based Versus Markerless Kinematic Inputs
items.abstract: Musculoskeletal (MSK) modeling is widely used to estimate spinal loading. However, conventional modeling pipelines are computationally intensive and time-consuming, which limit their application for workplace injury risk assessment. This study developed a machine learning (ML) model to predict lumbosacral compression force using intermediate outputs from an MSK modeling workflow. Twenty-one participants completed lifting tasks while marker-based and markerless kinematics were recorded. Reference compression forces were obtained from completed OpenSim simulations, and the resulting dataset was used to train the ML model using three input feature sets. The best-performing model achieved mean root mean square errors of 3.0% with marker-based inputs and 9.9% with markerless inputs. These findings suggest that combining ML with conventional MSK modeling can enable rapid spinal load prediction and may support field deployment when coupled with markerless motion capture. However, given the higher errors observed with markerless input, future work is needed to improve the kinematics accuracy of the markerless system.
