items.title: A Random Forest-Based AI Decision Support System for an Integrated Indonesian Civil Service Information System
items.abstract: Digital transformation in public administration increases the need for personnel information systems that can consolidate fragmented civil-service records and turn them into timely, transparent, and actionable decision support. This study developed SIPINTAR (Integrated, Adaptive, and Responsive Interactive Personnel Intelligence System), an artificial intelligence-based platform designed to integrate civil-service personnel information and support administrative decision-making within an Indonesian government institution. The study adopted a Research and Development approach and implemented the system through a Waterfall-based Software Development Life Cycle. Personnel data from multiple source systems, representing 5,320 civil servants and more than 42,000 historical records for 2019–2025, were integrated using Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) and Extract, Transform, and Load (ETL) processes. The integrated data were then subjected to cleaning, transformation, feature engineering, and Random Forest modeling. Model performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score, whereas system acceptance was examined through a User Acceptance Test. The strongest reported result was obtained for employee-performance prediction, with 87.24% accuracy, 86% precision, 85% recall, and 85.5% F1-score. Feature-importance analysis as the explainable artificial intelligence component identified performance score, competency level, and years of service as the three most influential variables. The integrated dashboard and AI Assistant provided consolidated access to analytical information, and the UAT result reached 91.40%. Overall, the findings suggest that SIPINTAR can move personnel information management beyond historical record keeping toward predictive and explainable decision support. Nevertheless, the results should be validated with baseline models and broader institutional datasets before being generalized across agencies.

items.abstract: The purpose of this review is to examine the diagnostic challenges arising from the mathematical biases of the DAS28 index used in monitoring rheumatoid arthritis, as well as the psychological and neurobiological factors underlying patient-physician discordance. Furthermore, this paper aims to analyze the role of digital biomarkers in future decision-making. A structural characteristic of the DAS28 index is that its subjective components carry twice the weight of objective metrics. In cases of central sensitization, depression, or anxiety, this can result in "false-positive" disease activity, leading to unjustified and costly interventions, as well as ineffective therapy. Literature confirms that patient-physician discordance is one of the primary predictors of therapeutic failure, particularly in difficult-to-treat (D2T) cases. The application of the DAS28-P index can help identify pain-dominant phenotypes. Besides musculoskeletal ultrasound, new technologies, such as keystroke dynamics analysis or artificial intelligence-based imaging, offer objective measures to eliminate subjective biases. Modern rheumatological approaches should integrate psychological support, patient education, and pain modulation alongside immunosuppressive treatment. The implementation of digital biomarkers and hybrid care models not only improves the patient's quality of life but also generates significant system-level cost savings in healthcare. items.title: A Survey of Agentic AI: Architectures, Reasoning, Planning, Memory, Collaboration, and Real-World Applications
items.abstract: Agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI) is a new paradigm that allows intelligent systems to behave independently, pursue specific objectives, and adapt to changing circumstances. Agentic AI combines reasoning, planning, memory, learning, and tool utilization to do complicated tasks with minimal human involvement, in contrast to traditional AI systems that mainly react to user inputs. In this article, takes a look at Agentic AI from every angle: its theoretical underpinnings, technological supports, architectural blueprints, and real-world uses. Many models and frameworks are covered, including cognitive and modular designs, systems based on reinforcement learning, hybrid models, and multi-agent systems. Symbolic, probabilistic, and self-reflective reasoning are some of the reasoning methodologies covered. Classical, hierarchical, and adaptive planning strategies are also covered. Agents' ability to reliably and efficiently execute tasks is investigated by looking at memory management, communication protocols, coordination mechanisms, and collaborative decision-making. A wide range of business, medical, financial, academic, and personal aid apps are evaluated in the poll. Privacy, security, computational costs, scalability, and unexpected behavior are the main issues that are highlighted in the end. The study emphasizes the need for more investigation into how to create Agentic AI systems that are reliable, flexible, and effective.

items.title: Abdurauf Fitrat's term-formation principles and the semantic-functional adaptation of artificial intelligence terms into Uzbek
items.abstract: This article compares Abdurauf Fitrat’s principles of terminology formation with contemporary strategies for adapting English artificial intelligence terminology into Uzbek. Its objective is to develop qualitative criteria for evaluating terminological equivalents in relation to meaning, linguistic structure, and communicative use. The material comprises seven selected expressions: artificial intelligence, machine learning, deep learning, neural network, prompt, chatbot, and large language model. Comparative, componential, word formation, and functional pragmatic methods are employed. The analysis distinguishes calquing, direct borrowing, hybrid nomination, and descriptive rendering. It shows that formal similarity to an English source expression does not necessarily guarantee conceptual accuracy or accessibility for readers. The interpretation of prompt depends on context. Fitrat’s linguistic legacy is treated as a historical comparative perspective rather than direct evidence of continuity with digital terminology. A four criterion assessment framework is proposed, covering conceptual precision, structural compatibility, communicative transparency, and terminological consistency. These qualitative conclusions require corpus verification. The framework may inform terminology development.

items.title: ADOPTION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN SUPPLY CHAIN MANAGEMENT: BARRIERS AND ENABLERS IN DEVELOPING ECONOMIES
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative technology capable of enhancing efficiency, decision-making, and resilience in supply chain management. However, its adoption in developing economies remains constrained by several technological, organizational, and environmental challenges. This study examined the adoption of Artificial Intelligence in supply chain management, with emphasis on the barriers and enablers in developing economies, using Nigeria as the study context. A cross-sectional survey research design was adopted, and data were collected from 235 employees, managers, and supply chain professionals in selected manufacturing firms, logistics companies, retail organizations, and small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria using a structured questionnaire titled Artificial Intelligence Adoption in Supply Chain Management Index (AIASCMI). Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and Pearson Product Moment Correlation. The findings revealed that identified barriers, including inadequate digital infrastructure, high implementation costs, shortage of skilled personnel, and organizational challenges, have a significant negative relationship with the adoption of Artificial Intelligence in supply chain management. The study also found that identified enablers, such as top management support, technological readiness, employee competence, and government support, significantly influence the successful adoption of Artificial Intelligence. The study concludes that overcoming existing barriers while strengthening organizational and technological capabilities is essential for the successful adoption of Artificial Intelligence in supply chain management. It is recommended that organizations invest in digital infrastructure, workforce development, and supportive management practices to maximize the benefits of Artificial Intelligence and improve supply chain performance.

items.title: ADOPTION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN SUPPLY CHAIN MANAGEMENT: BARRIERS AND ENABLERS IN DEVELOPING ECONOMIES
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative technology capable of enhancing efficiency, decision-making, and resilience in supply chain management. However, its adoption in developing economies remains constrained by several technological, organizational, and environmental challenges. This study examined the adoption of Artificial Intelligence in supply chain management, with emphasis on the barriers and enablers in developing economies, using Nigeria as the study context. A cross-sectional survey research design was adopted, and data were collected from 235 employees, managers, and supply chain professionals in selected manufacturing firms, logistics companies, retail organizations, and small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria using a structured questionnaire titled Artificial Intelligence Adoption in Supply Chain Management Index (AIASCMI). Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and Pearson Product Moment Correlation. The findings revealed that identified barriers, including inadequate digital infrastructure, high implementation costs, shortage of skilled personnel, and organizational challenges, have a significant negative relationship with the adoption of Artificial Intelligence in supply chain management. The study also found that identified enablers, such as top management support, technological readiness, employee competence, and government support, significantly influence the successful adoption of Artificial Intelligence. The study concludes that overcoming existing barriers while strengthening organizational and technological capabilities is essential for the successful adoption of Artificial Intelligence in supply chain management. It is recommended that organizations invest in digital infrastructure, workforce development, and supportive management practices to maximize the benefits of Artificial Intelligence and improve supply chain performance.

items.title: Agentic Artificial Intelligence as a Digital Employee: Redefining the Boundaries of Delegation, Accountability, and Control in Information Systems-Enabled Organizations
items.abstract: Background and Purpose: The rapid transition from deterministic automation and passive algorithmic decision-support systems to agentic artificial intelligence (Agentic AI) represents an unprecedented ontological shift in enterprise information systems (IS). Unlike antecedent generative models that merely synthesize conversational text, agentic AI operates with persistent internal memory, autonomous multi-step cognitive reasoning, goal decomposition, and self-directed tool and API execution. In contemporary digital organizations, these autonomous systems are progressively onboarded, provisioned, and treated not merely as passive software artifacts, but as synthetic workers or "digital employees." However, this conceptual elevation fractures foundational organizational assumptions rooted in classical agency theory, sociotechnical systems theory, and managerial control architectures. This monograph investigates how enterprise deployment of digital employees redefines the boundaries of delegation, moral and organizational accountability, and managerial control within IS-enabled organizational environments. Design, Methodology, and Approach: To rigorously interrogate this emergent socio-algorithmic reality, an extensive explanatory mixed-methods research design was executed across a 24-month longitudinal investigation (2024-2026). The quantitative phase collected and analyzed empirical survey data from 482 senior enterprise leaders, Chief Information Officers (CIOs), Chief AI Officers (CAIOs), Enterprise Architects, and line managers across four knowledge-intensive industry verticals (Financial Services & FinTech, Healthcare & HealthTech, Global Supply Chain Logistics, and Enterprise Cloud/SaaS). Structural Equation Modeling using Partial Least Squares (PLS-SEM) was employed to empirically test the structural dependencies between perceived agentic autonomy, algorithmic trust, delegation depth, operational agility, and accountability drift. The qualitative phase comprised 38 semi-structured, in-depth key-informant interviews and four comprehensive, longitudinal multi-case studies examining end-to-end organizational deployments of multi-agent architectures (including LangGraph, AutoGen, CrewAI, and proprietary enterprise agent meshes). Rigorous thematic analysis and qualitative comparative synthesis were conducted to deconstruct operational failures, behavioral drift phenomena, and governance adaptations. Empirical Findings: The empirical results reveal a profound structural paradox in enterprise agentic delegation. First, the transition from "task offloading" to "autonomous mandate delegation" generates a statistically significant positive effect on organizational agility (β=0.495, p<0.001) and operational velocity, but concurrently fuels a critical "accountability void" and organizational drift (β=0.342, p<0.001). Second, traditional managerial control frameworks specifically diagnostic and boundary controls suffer severe operational degradation when confronted with non-deterministic agentic planning and recursive API invocation. Third, human supervisors frequently exhibit either "cognitive abandonment" (over-trusting autonomous agents due to perceived competence) or severe "algorithmic cynicism" (resorting to micro-surveillance that negates agentic throughput benefits). Fourth, the investigation reveals the emergence of what we conceptualize as the "Synthetic Moral Crumple Zone," wherein middle-tier human managers are held legally and administratively accountable for unforeseen agentic systemic errors that they possessed neither the technical visibility nor the temporal window to prevent.

items.title: AI and the Shift in Power Dynamics in English Language Education: Portfolios as Tools for Authentic Self-Agency and Self-Determination
items.abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in English language education is reshaping traditional pedagogical frameworks, fostering learner autonomy, and redefining the educator’s role. This article presents a conceptual framework and pedagogical model exploring how AI-driven portfolio assessment and custom AI language models can be integrated within an Agile learning framework to support iterative, self-directed learning. While AI enhances language acquisition through personalized feedback and adaptive learning, concerns about authenticity, plagiarism, and over-reliance on AI-generated content remain. A structured approach to AI literacy development is introduced, ensuring that students critically assess AI-generated feedback rather than passively accepting it. A key component of this framework is AI-supported reflection, where learners evaluate AI suggestions based on alignment with their authentic voice and intended meaning. This process is reinforced through an AI-reflection rubric designed to cultivate metacognitive awareness and critical engagement with AI outputs. Agile methodologies, particularly iterative learning cycles, scaffold AI-supported writing assignments, balancing human and AI feedback for progressive skill development. The article also examines configurable AI tools for assessment, such as custom GPTs within ChatGPT and Gems within Google Gemini, which can evaluate language proficiency, track learning progression, and facilitate AI-supported peer assessment. The framework is designed to be adaptable across international EFL and ESL contexts, supporting authentic learning rather than replacing the learner’s central role in the learning process.

items.title: AI CHAT ASSISTANT FOR ONLINE BUSINESS
items.abstract: Online businesses must answer product questions, explain policies, guide purchases and resolve order-related concerns across multiplechannels. Human-only support can be costly and slow during peak demand, while rigid rule-based chatbots struggle with varied wording andmulti-step questions. This paper presents a conceptual design for an Artificial Intelligence (AI) Chat Assistant for Online Business thatcombines natural language understanding, retrieval from approved business knowledge, controlled access to commerce services andescalation to human staff. The proposed assistant interprets customer intent, retrieves relevant product and policy information, generatesgrounded responses, and invokes permitted actions such as checking order status only after appropriate authentication. The architectureemphasizes factual consistency, privacy, security, accessibility and measurable service quality. It also describes a developmentmethodology, evaluation metrics, risk controls and a staged deployment plan. Since this is a design-oriented study, no original performanceresults are claimed; the proposed evaluation must be conducted using representative customer queries and verified business data.

items.title: AI DRIVEN DIGITAL TWINS FOR DRUG REPURPOSING: CURRENT EVIDENCES, APPLICATIONS, TRANSLATIONAL CHALLENGES AND FUTURE DIRECTIONS
items.abstract: Conventional drug discovery and development is associated with substantial financial costs, lengthy development timelines, and high attrition rates during preclinical and clinical evaluation. Drug repurposing provides an alternative strategy by identifying new therapeutic applications for existing drugs with previously characterized pharmacological and safety profiles. Recent advances in artificial intelligence, multimodal biomedical data integration, mechanistic modelling, and digital twin technology have created new opportunities to improve computational drug repurposing and patient-specific treatment prediction. This review examines the emerging integration of AI-driven digital twins with drug repurposing, focusing on digital twin architectures, artificial intelligence methodologies multi modal data integration, drug target prediction, pharmacokinetic or pharmacodynamic modelling, treatment-response simulation, and personalized therapeutic decision-making. The review also discusses applications across cancer, neurodegenerative, cardiovascular, infectious, metabolic, and rare diseases. Particular emphasis is placed on the development of patient-specific digital twins, integration of multi-omics and clinical data, virtual treatment simulation, and validation through computational, experimental, and clinical approaches. Major challenges include data heterogeneity, interoperability, model reliability, uncertainty quantification, interpretability, algorithmic bias, cybersecurity, privacy, clinical workflow integration, and regulatory acceptance. Emerging approaches, including causal AI, federated learning, multimodal foundation models, virtual clinical trials, and real-time adaptive digital twins, may further enhance the translational potential of AI-enabled drug repurposing. However, prospective clinical validation and standardized regulatory frameworks remain necessary before widespread clinical implementation.

items.title: AI Governance In India: A Critical Examination Of Digital Rights, Constitutional Safeguards And Legal Accountability
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence currently determines how individuals access information, services and decisions from institutions. The influence of this technology raises questions about how the law can hold those who control such power accountable under the constitution. In this article I investigate if the developing governance framework in India protects digital rights and offers ways to fix harm caused by artificial intelligence. It applies to a qualitative doctrinal method to examine constitutional guarantees, court decisions, laws plus official policies. To assist this analysis, the text includes a comparison of two international instruments. The discussion distinguishes between constitutional duties, laws that the state has passed but not fully started, secondary regulations and governance principles that lack binding force. I argue that protecting privacy does not solve the problems of unfair classification, hidden decision processes, or deception. Privacy laws do not address how companies spread responsibility across long supply chains. India uses a strategy that focuses on innovation and treats different industries separately - this method is flexible, but it is only legitimate if the state provides rules for fair procedures but also ways for citizens to complain. In response, I propose a framework for constitutional accountability - this framework connects the requirement for a legal basis, the balance of interests, equal treatment and clear explanations. It also requires that a human reviews decisions and that victims receive a fix for their injuries. The specific recommendations include tests to see how important uses of technology affect society. There must be records that allow independent experts to check the system. On top of this the state must use safeguards when it buys technology. Responsibility is assigned to the party who controls risks that they can predict.

items.title: AI Governance: What Exactly Are We Governing?
items.abstract: WP_AI_8.5 develops a three-object framework for clarifying what AI governance is actually governing. The paper begins from a structural problem in contemporary AI governance. Technical systems, human decision-makers, institutional actors, oversight mechanisms, accountability, safety, and responsibility are often discussed within the same governance language without clearly separating the objects to which those rules apply. This can produce governance object drift, in which the focus of governance shifts during analysis, and governance subject inversion, in which AI becomes increasingly personalized as the apparent actor while the humans and institutions exercising real authority become less visible. The paper identifies three distinct but connected objects of AI governance. The first is the AI entity itself. The paper distinguishes four governance identities: Tool, System, Agent, and Autonomous Actor. These categories are not claims about consciousness or legal personhood. They describe different operational relationships between AI capability, delegated authority, persistence, external consequence, and human reauthorization. The second object is the human authority structure across the AI lifecycle. Developers, testers, providers, approvers, regulators, administrators, operators, and users exercise different forms of authority and therefore require different forms of governance. Human conduct must remain a direct object of AI governance rather than being displaced by anthropomorphic descriptions of AI behavior. The third object is the institutional interface through which AI capability enters society. Admission, authorization, release, deployment, access, supervision, review, restriction, suspension, and withdrawal determine how technical capability becomes socially operative. The paper also distinguishes Governance Identity Drift from Governance Object Drift. The former occurs when an AI system’s actual operational identity changes while its formal governance category remains unchanged. The latter occurs when governance itself shifts its analytical object, for example when a human authorization decision is gradually redescribed as autonomous machine behavior. The central argument is that governance must define its own objects rather than inherit them passively from technical narratives. AI should be governed according to what kind of operational entity it is. Humans and institutions should be governed according to the authority they exercise. The human-AI institutional interface should be governed according to the social consequences it enables. WP_AI_8.5 builds on the preceding papers in the WP_AI_8 series. WP_AI_8.1 established the engineering circuit-breaker principle; WP_AI_8.2 examined responsibility escape; WP_AI_8.3 developed a dual-track framework connecting capability control and human responsibility; and WP_AI_8.4 addressed the conditions under which AI capability may move from controlled development into social release. WP_AI_8.5 moves one level upward by clarifying the governance objects to which those mechanisms apply.

items.title: AI in HRM: a unified model of AI capabilities and process efficiency for enhanced HRM effectiveness
items.abstract: Abstract The accelerating adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in human resource management (HRM) raises important questions about which AI-driven interventions most effectively enhance workforce agility, decision-making, and employee outcomes. This study investigated the effects of multiple AI applications—including employee wellbeing (AIEEW), performance management (AIPM), recruitment and selection (AIRS), training and development (AITD), and strategic HR practices (AISHRP), on HR process efficiency (HRPE), decision-making agility (DMA), workplace AI integration (WAI), and enhanced HRM effectiveness (EHRE). Data was collected from 256 professionals in organizational and educational institutions and analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) with SmartPLS. Results revealed that eight of nine hypothesized paths were supported, with AI-enabled wellbeing exerting the strongest effect on workplace AI integration (β = 0.583, p < .001). Recruitment and performance management systems significantly enhanced HR process efficiency, while strategic HR planning and talent analytics improved decision-making agility. HR performance enhancement strongly predicted HR effectiveness (β = 0.458, p < .001), highlighting process efficiency as a key mediator of AI’s impact. Two paths were weaker: AI in training and development did not significantly affect HR process efficiency, and decision-making agility showed only marginal influence on HRM effectiveness. Theoretically, the study enriches the Resource-Based View and Dynamic Capabilities Theory by demonstrating how AI functions as both a strategic resource and a capability-building tool. Practically, findings suggest that organizations should prioritize wellbeing, recruitment, and HR performance systems when investing in AI, while ensuring that training platforms and decision-support tools are better integrated into HR processes.

items.title: AI in mathematics classrooms: a synergistic strategy for diversity and inclusivity
items.abstract: Despite growing emphasis on inclusive education, mathematics classrooms still exhibit disparities arising from cognitive, linguistic, socioeconomic, and systemic barriers, marginalizing diverse students and limiting equitable learning opportunities. Artificial intelligence (AI) presents considerable potential for addressing these challenges. This study investigates how AI technologies can be harnessed to create mathematics classrooms that are inclusive and adaptive to individual student needs. Anchored in Universal Design for Learning (UDL) and the Substitution, Augmentation, Modification, Redefinition (SAMR) frameworks, the study explores how AI functionalities can facilitate personalized learning, responsive instruction, and equitable participation. The study employs a hybrid conceptual–structured narrative review approach, synthesizing existing literature through structured searching, screening, thematic coding, and conceptual integration. The synthesis examines AI functionalities, inclusive pedagogical affordances, implementation challenges, ethical and equity concerns, and future directions. On this basis, the study develops the Synergistic AI-Inclusive Mathematics Education (SAIME) framework, conceptualizing UDL as an inclusion-oriented design foundation, SAMR as a technological transformation pathway, and teacher-mediated pedagogy and ethical safeguards as essential conditions for equitable outcomes in access, participation, and achievement. It concludes that AI can contribute meaningfully to inclusive mathematics education when its technological affordances are purposefully aligned with inclusive pedagogy, ethical and equity safeguards, and equitable learning goals.

items.title: AI Redefines Next-Gen Drilling Vibration Compliance
items.abstract: _ This case study from Tomax outlines the use of artificial intelligence to analyze high-fidelity data of the full drilling process. The problem of downhole vibrations remains a significant barrier for the drilling industry. An emerging technology based on direct interception of disturbing resonances is now being used to address the issue. Such solutions rely on a new level of understanding with respect to the true bottomhole assembly (BHA) dynamics. Artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) techniques are now helping deliver the full picture. While the specific product development in this field belongs in the commercial space, the necessity for more and better data on drilling dynamics is commonplace. This case study describes a successful solution for data harvesting on a level that is both new and found to meet requirement for the application of AI/ML solutions. The study concludes with examples from analysis that reveal the potential from a true image of everything going on in a drillstring. Reinventing Drilling Dynamics Traditional analysis of drilling dynamics frequently references data from downhole accelerometers. However, these systems typically capture a mix of effects rather than the underlying coupling of forces that cause resonances and, consequently, poor performance and downtime from failures. The fundamentals of these resonances reside in the transfer of torsional and axial forces from surface to the bit. On most rigs, the surface input and reactive loads are recorded at sparse intervals (typically every 10 seconds or longer). Capturing this critical information at a high-fidelity level in this environment presents two critical challenges: - Signal Integrity: Eliminating data corruption and packet loss from intermittent transfer when sampling frequencies exceeding 1,000 Hz using RF from a rotating shaft in a rough environment. - Data Pipeline: While modern sensor assemblies can export structural acoustics and stress waves at extreme sample rates, the bottleneck is the data pipeline and the requirement for a continuous stream of megabytes of time-stamped data every second into a usable database.

items.title: AI-ASSISTED UV–VISIBLE SPECTROSCOPY FOR RAPID QUANTIFICATION OF PHARMACEUTICAL DRUGS
items.abstract: UV–Visible (UV–Vis) spectrophotometry is a rapid, economical and widely available technique for pharmaceutical analysis, but its selectivity is limited when the drugs in a formulation have overlapping absorption spectra. The integration of chemometrics and artificial intelligence (AI), including machine learning (ML) algorithms such as partial least squares (PLS), principal component regression (PCR), support vector regression (SVR), artificial neural networks (ANN) and random forests, with intelligent wavelength selection and metaheuristic optimization (genetic and Firefly algorithms), allows the simultaneous quantification of several active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) from the whole spectrum rather than a single wavelength. This review summarizes the principles of UV–Vis spectroscopy, the current status of AI-assisted UV–Vis analysis, and the challenges related to model interpretability, data integrity, validation and instrument variability. Applications, drawbacks and futureprospects are discussed, including process analytical technology (PAT), portable instruments, green analytical chemistry and regulatory acceptance of AI-enabled spectroscopic methods as complementary tools to chromatographic assays in pharmaceutical quality control.

items.abstract: Software development often requires programmers to write repetitive code, understand unfamiliar requirements, and spend considerabletime identifying and correcting errors. Recent advances in artificial intelligence have enabled systems to generate source code fromnatural-language instructions. However, generated code may contain syntax errors, incorrect logic, insecure patterns, or incompletehandling of edge cases. This paper proposes an AI-Based Code Generation and Self-Testing System that accepts a programming task innatural language, generates a candidate solution, prepares or selects test cases, executes the code in a controlled environment, and analysesthe results. The proposed workflow combines prompt interpretation, code generation, static validation, test-case generation, sandboxedexecution, and feedback-based refinement. The system is intended to support developers and learners by reducing repetitive effort andproviding an initial validation cycle. It does not replace code review or guarantee correctness; execution safety, test coverage, modellimitations, and human verification remain important. This paper presents a proposed methodology and evaluation plan. Quantitativeperformance claims should be added only after implementation and testing.

items.title: AI-Based Customer Service and Brand Loyalty in Saudi Retail: An Empirical Investigation of the Service Quality–Emotional Attachment–Loyalty Pathway in 2025–2026
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-powered customer service systems have expanded across Saudi Arabia’s retail sector during 2025–2026, with major retailers increasingly exploring chatbots, recommendation engines, and automated service technologies. Official Saudi digital-economy statistics document the wider shift towards digital commerce, although online-shopping participation should not be interpreted as a direct measure of AI adoption or retailer-specific investment. This study examines the relationship among AI service quality, emotional brand attachment, and brand loyalty using survey results reported for 512 retail customers in Riyadh, Jeddah, and Dammam, collected between May and September 2026. Using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) and bootstrap resampling, the analysis reports a positive direct association between AI service quality and loyalty (β = 0.421, p < 0.001), together with a positive indirect association through emotional brand attachment (reported indirect effect = 0.238, 95% CI [0.187, 0.289]). The study considers a possible “mechanical efficiency paradox”: functional improvements in AI service may be more strongly associated with loyalty than with emotional attachment. Importantly, this survey does not include a direct comparison with human-delivered service, and the reported positive attachment coefficient (β = 0.187) cannot establish that AI decreases attachment. The reported gender subgroup estimates differ: the AI quality–attachment association is positive for male respondents (β = 0.289, p = 0.001) and statistically nonsignificant for female respondents (β = −0.023, p = 0.811). Age-specific estimates also vary, with more positive reported coefficients in younger groups, although the statistical significance of the age differences requires further supporting output. The manuscript reports that the model accounts for 51.2% of the variance in loyalty (R2 = 0.512) and has positive predictive relevance (Q2 = 0.289). Because some path estimates, correlations, and variance-explained values are not mutually consistent, these results require rechecking against the original SmartPLS output before publication. Managerial implications include offering hybrid AI–human service, allowing customers to choose their preferred channel, and maintaining personal attention for complex or emotionally sensitive interactions. The findings provide a framework for assessing how technological service quality and relationship-building might jointly contribute to brand loyalty.

items.title: AI-DRIVEN DIGITAL MARKETING STRATEGIES IN THE PHARMACEUTICAL INDUSTRY: OPPORTUNITIES, CHALLENGES, AND FUTURE PERSPECTIVES
items.abstract: Pharmaceutical marketing is being reshaped by the growing use of digital technologies and artificial intelligence (AI) in communication, customer engagement, and commercial decision-making. Promotion that once relied almost entirely on medical representatives, face-to-face physician visits, product detailing, and printed material is now supplemented, and in some cases reshaped, by digital platforms, social media, e-detailing, webinars, data analytics, and omnichannel communication. This review looks at how AI is being applied to pharmaceutical digital marketing, with particular attention to machine learning, predictive analytics, segmentation of customers and healthcare professionals, personalized communication, customer relationship management, generative AI, and omnichannel engagement. Evidence from the published literature suggests that digital channels widen the reach and flexibility of pharmaceutical communication, while AI adds the ability to analyse large datasets, anticipate behaviour, segment audiences, and personalize content at scale. At the same time, this shift brings its own set of problems: data privacy, inconsistent data quality, algorithmic bias, the risk of misinformation, limited transparency, regulatory compliance, and the continued need for human oversight all surface repeatedly in the literature. Empirical studies also indicate that digital engagement can shape how healthcare professionals are communicated with, influence prescribing-related behaviour, and affect consumer attitudes, though the size of this effect depends heavily on the channel, audience, and therapeutic area involved. Taken together, the evidence points toward a future in which human expertise, digital communication, and AI-supported decision-making work alongside one another rather than one replacing the other. For this model to be sustainable, pharmaceutical marketing will need to be built on responsible implementation, ethical communication, evidence-based content, and clear governance.

items.title: AI-Empowered Teaching of Senior High School English Practical Writing: A “5A+E” Mechanism and Five-Stage Pathway Design
items.abstract: Practical writing is an important component of senior high school English teaching. he English Curriculum Standards for Senior High School (2017 edition, 2020 revision) requires students to select appropriate language forms according to the identity of the communicative partner, he occasion and the degree of formality, o as to achieve effective cross-cultural communication. owever, urrent practical writing teaching in Grade 10 still suffers from mechanical format training, eak reader awareness, nappropriate register control, nd single and delayed feedback. Although generative artificial intelligence offers new possibilities for writing instruction, existing studies have focused mainly on automated essay scoring, academic writing at the tertiary level, or continuation writing tasks, and few have systematically constructed an AI-empowered mechanism and teaching pathway for senior high school practical writing from the perspective of the integration of teaching, learning and assessment. Adopting a conceptual construction and lesson design orientation, and grounded in the cognitive process theory of writing,t he technology-enhanced language learning framework, self-efficacy theory and formative assessment theory, this study proposes a “5A+E” empowerment mechanism model, comprising Analysis, Activation, Assistance, Assessment, Adaptation, and Ethics. On this basis, a five-stage teaching pathway—context trigger, element deconstruction, AI co-writing, multi-dimensional evaluation, and reflective transfer—is designed, and a lesson on the invitation letter for the “Chinese Culture Festival” is presented. The study argues that AI can serve as a reader analyst, format validator, point generator, register regulator and evaluation embedder, moving practical writing instruction from template drilling toward authentic communication. As a theoretical construction and lesson design study, this paper has not yet been empirically tested; future action research or quasi-experimental studies are needed to validate and refine the model and pathway.

items.title: AI-Enabled Public Grievance Redressal: A Framework for Citizen-Centric Responsiveness in Indian States
items.abstract: Grievance redressal is where citizens test whether government listens. Indian governments receive millions of complaints each year through portals, call centres, social media, letters and in-person visits. The volume, the variety of languages and the number of departments involved make it hard to route complaints correctly, resolve them on time and learn from patterns. Artificial intelligence (AI), and in particular natural language processing for Indian languages, can help with each of these steps — but only if it is introduced with clear safeguards and with officers, not algorithms, remaining accountable for decisions. This paper proposes a five-layer framework for AI-enabled grievance redressal in Indian states: (1) multilingual, multichannel intake; (2) classification, routing and prioritisation; (3) officer assistance for resolution; (4) closure verification and citizen feedback; and (5) analytics for root-cause and policy learning. For each layer it sets out what AI can do, the human checks required and suitable performance measures. It also discusses governance, data protection and change-management requirements, and suggests a phased path from pilot to state-wide adoption. The paper is a design framework drawn from e-governance practice and the published literature; it does not report results from a deployed system.

items.abstract: The continued growth of mobile data traffic is placing increasing demands on radio access networks (RANs).Although 4G and 5G networks already use sophisticated automation to manage radio resources, conventionaloptimisation methods can struggle to respond efficiently to rapidly changing traffic patterns, complex interferenceconditions and variations in user behaviour. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) offer an opportunityto make network management more predictive by identifying patterns in network data, forecasting demand andsupporting more adaptive resource allocation. This article examines the development of AI-native RAN, focusing onthe UK 5G environment. It reviews radio resource management, predictive optimisation and emerging AI-RANarchitectures, including the O-RAN Intelligent Controller framework. It considers the O2–Nokia live deploymentannounced at London Paddington in October 2026 and BT's planned AI-RAN trial with Nokia and NVIDIA inBirmingham during 2027. It also examines data quality, model reliability, security, interoperability, computingoverhead and human oversight. The article argues that AI-native RAN should be treated as an evolution ofestablished radio engineering, with benefits demonstrated through measurable improvements in network efficiency,reliability and customer experience.

items.title: Algorithmic Bias in HR Management: A Critical Inquiry into the Automation of Inequity
items.abstract: This paper provides a comprehensive critical analysis of algorithmic bias in human resource management, examining how artificial intelligence (AI) systems used in hiring, promotions, and performance management can perpetuate and amplify societal biases. Moving beyond conventional discussions of bias, this research introduces a series of novel theoretical frameworks to uncover the deeper, systemic mechanisms through which algorithmic HR systems produce inequitable outcomes. These include the Sociotechnical Bias Amplification Model (SBAM), which explains how temporal bias, intersectional bias, and feedback loops interact to compound discrimination; the Algorithmic Opacity Paradox, which argues that the perceived objectivity of AI obscures its discriminatory potential; and the Fairness Impossibility Theorem in the HR context, which demonstrates the mathematical and normative trade-offs inherent in any algorithmic fairness definition. The paper further develops a critical perspective by introducing concepts such as data colonialism, the performance management panopticon, and the algorithmic accountability gap. Through a synthesis of technical literature, organizational theory, and critical algorithm studies, this research argues that the challenge of algorithmic bias is not merely a technical problem of “debiasing” but a fundamental crisis of legitimacy for automated decision-making in the workplace. The analysis is supported by clearly labelled conceptual diagrams and selected empirical findings drawn from published research. It concludes with a set of actionable recommendations for HR leaders, policymakers, and researchers, advocating for a shift from a technical-fix mindset to a more holistic, human-centered approach to governance that prioritizes justice, accountability, and equity.

items.title: An outlook on varied ecological engineering solutions for landslide prevention
items.abstract: This review assesses ecological engineering solutions for landslide prevention and slope stabilization by synthesizing evidence identified through scientific databases. The review encompasses the idea of applying vegetation-based techniques, including live stakes, brush layering, revegetation, grasses, herbaceous plants, bamboo plantations, and lithophytic life forms, together with conventional and structural measures such as natural geotextiles, live wooden crib walls, wattle fences, live silt fences, and live gully breaks. The reviewed evidence highlights the importance of species with strong root systems, which can influence the effectiveness of bioengineering interventions. Species such as Vetiver, Bermuda Grass, Ryegrass, Alder, selected Ficus species, and bamboo show deep-rooted control over soil reinforcement, erosion, and slope stabilization, while lithophytic life forms and pioneer colonizers may support the restoration of exposed rocky and landslide-affected surfaces. The review also examines the contribution of artificial intelligence, remote sensing, unmanned aerial vehicles, LiDAR, interferometric synthetic aperture radar, and machine learning models in landslide susceptibility assessment, monitoring, and advance warning. Overall, the findings revealed that integrated ecological engineering and data-driven monitoring may complement conventional stabilization measures, reduce landslide risk, restore degraded slopes, and inform sustainable land-management planning.

items.title: Analisis Faktor-Faktor Retensi Karyawan Kontrak pada Divisi Operasional di PT XYZ
items.abstract: This research is motivated by the high turnover of contract employees in the Operational Division of PT. XYZ which has an impact on increasing recruitment needs, disrupting company operations, and decreasing productivity. The study aims to analyze employee retention factors including organizational components, career opportunities, rewards, job design, and employee relations. The method used is a qualitative approach supported by descriptive analysis using the Weight Mean Score (WMS). Data were collected through observation, questionnaires to 61 contract employees, semi-structured interviews with five informants, and documentation. Data analysis was carried out through data reduction, data presentation, drawing conclusions, and WMS analysis. The results of the study indicate that all factors are in the good category, namely organizational components (3.66), career opportunities (3.58), rewards (3.68), job design (3.62), and employee relations (3.52). However, the company still needs to improve work facilities, transparency of promotions and career paths, fairness of rewards, job variety, and communication between superiors and employees. The study concludes that these five factors contribute to supporting contract employee retention at PT. XYZ.

items.title: Application of Management Information Systems and Artificial Intelligence in the Governance of Islamic Education
items.abstract: This study investigates the implementation of Management Information Systems (MIS) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Islamic education governance at MIN 9 Magetan. Driven by digital transformation demands, the research aims to analyze the integration of these technologies, identify supporting and inhibiting factors, and evaluate their impact on educational service quality. Employing a qualitative case study design, data were collected through observations, in-depth interviews, and documentation, and analyzed using the interactive model of Miles, Huberman, and Saldaña. The findings reveal that the deployment of specific MIS platforms, such as EMIS 4.0 and ERKAM, significantly enhances administrative efficiency, financial transparency, and data-driven decision-making by the madrasah leadership. Concurrently, the grassroots adoption of AI tools, including ChatGPT, Gemini, and Canva AI, empowers teachers to accelerate lesson planning, design Higher Order Thinking Skills (HOTS) assessments, and foster pedagogical innovation through interactive learning media. While visionary leadership commitment and adequate digital infrastructure strongly support this transformation, several challenges persist. These include a digital literacy gap among senior educators experiencing cultural resistance, as well as operational disruptions caused by central server instability during critical data synchronization periods. Ultimately, the synergistic integration of MIS and AI positively impacts service quality, transparency, and accountability. Therefore, prioritizing targeted digital literacy programs and allocating dedicated budgets for comprehensive AI training are recommended to ensure sustainable implementation. This study contributes to the development of a modern Islamic education governance model that harmonizes digital technology, human resource competence, and good governance principles grounded in Islamic values.

items.title: ARTIFICAL INTELLIGENCE AND MACHINE LEARNING IN PHARMACEUTICAL ANALYSIS
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) & Machine Learning (ML) are two terms that transformed pharmaceutical sciences, including drug discovery, drug development, precision medicine and nanomedicine. Traditional drug discovery is a long, expensive and failure-prone process that may take over 10 years and million of dollars before it produces a therapeutically active compound ready for clinical trials and commercialization. AI-driven computational approaches can tackle numerous challenges of drug discovery and development, including target or lead identification and optimization, virtual screening, predicting drug target interactions, toxicity and personalized treatment options. The concept of artificial intelligence was first introduced in the 1940s when Alan Turing laid the foundations for machine intelligence theory claiming that there is no fundamental difference between human and machine computation (Turing, 1950). The formal idea of artificial intelligence was further proposed by Mc Carthy, Minsky, Rochester and Shannon who proposed the Dartmouth Hypothesis about the possibility for machines to stimulate human intelligence (Mc Carthy et al 1955). In the following decades the concepts machine learning and deep learning were introduced Schmidhuber in 2015. There are three review papers that discuss the role of AI&ML in pharmaceutical sciences and health care. The first study focus on the role of artificial intelligence in drug discovery and discovery and precision nanomedicine (Zhu et al, 2022). Zhu et al. highlight importance of algorithms and nano-enabled therapeutics for precision nanomedicine. The main ideas of the study include finding and selecting the target developing the optimal drug using nano-enabled therapeutics and individualizing treatment based on patients characteristics. The second review paper discuss the role of AI in spatial structure of protein predicting and drug synergism prediction targeting molecular mechanism and protein drug interactions (Lie et al, 2022). The study by Lei et al. high-light the importance of AI in analyzing and prediction the spatial structure of protein to reveal molecular mechanisms and biological functions. The third review paper was discusses the concept of artificial intelligence, machine learning and deep learning elucidates ethical and social implications and high light the public awarness about AI (Garcia & Salichos, 2022). The study by Garcia & Salichosis a detailed analysis about the opportunities and limitations of AI.I would like to address the main ideas of all three reviewed papers and discuss hoe AL&ML can be applied to various stages of drug discovery and development. I will also comment on such terms as machine learning, deep learning, protein spatial structure prediction, virtual screening precision, precision medicine, nanomedicine, drug synergism prediction, explainable AI.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Patient–Healthcare Relationships: Psychosocial Perspective
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is becoming part of healthcare through tools that help organise medical information, support clinical decisions, answer common questions, and improve communication. These changes affect more than treatment and efficiency: they can also influence how patients feel, how much they trust healthcare professionals, and whether they feel heard and respected. This paper reviews AI in patient–healthcare relationships from a psychosocial perspective. It considers trust, empathy, privacy, patient autonomy, health literacy, anxiety, accessibility, and the role of clinicians in explaining AI-supported decisions. AI can make some services faster and easier to access, but it may also create distance when communication feels automated or when recommendations are difficult to understand. The paper argues that AI should strengthen—not replace—the human relationship at the centre of care. Responsible use requires transparency, protection of personal information, inclusive design, careful evaluation, and meaningful human oversight..

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and Audit Quality: Evidence from Emerging Economies
items.abstract: This study investigates the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) adoption on audit quality in emerging economies, with an emphasis on fraud detection, risk assessment, implementation challenges, and the roles of auditor competence and technological readiness. A quantitative research design was employed, using secondary panel data from 25 firms observed over a decade, yielding 250 firm-year observations. Data were drawn from annual reports, audit reports, governance disclosures, and publicly available financial statements. Analytical techniques included descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, fixed- and random-effects regression models, and Hausman specification tests to ensure methodological robustness. Findings reveal that AI adoption significantly enhances audit quality by improving fraud detection and risk assessment, enabling auditors to identify irregularities and unusual transactions more effectively. Nonetheless, weak technological infrastructure, high implementation costs, cybersecurity risks, and limited expertise constrain optimal adoption. Auditor competence and technological readiness emerged as decisive factors influencing AI’s effectiveness in improving audit outcomes. This study contributes to the literature by providing empirical evidence on AI’s transformative role in auditing within emerging economies, highlighting both opportunities and constraints. The findings underscore the need for investments in digital infrastructure, auditor training, and cybersecurity frameworks to maximize AI’s potential in audit practice.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and Older Persons: Opportunities for Empowerment and Risks of Digital Exclusion in Light of Rights-Based Safeguards
items.abstract: This study examines the relationship between the development of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies and the rights of older persons. It analyses the opportunities that smart applications offer in health care, independent living, social connection and economic security, set against the risks arising from digital exclusion, algorithmic age discrimination, privacy violations and fraud. The study adopts a descriptive-analytical approach based on international reports, systematic reviews, meta-analyses and relevant national surveys, and discusses the UAE legislative context. The review shows that the age gap in use remains wide, that the evidence of benefits is promising but limited, and that fraud risks are documented by rising figures. The study proposes a preliminary framework for safe digital empowerment that links graduated learning, inclusive design, data protection, human review and evaluation. It concludes that the rights-based value of AI is not measured by the mere availability of a service, but by its capacity to expand the real choices of older persons while respecting their will and dignity. The study does not present field results, nor does it claim to have tested the proposed model. items.title: Artificial Intelligence and Religious Policy: Ethical Governance in the Digital Public Sphere
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence increasingly mediates religious communication, knowledge, and participation in the digital public sphere, yet research remains fragmented across digital religion, human rights, and AI governance. This study examines how AI-mediated religious communication shapes authority, visibility, and participation; identifies associated ethical and rights-based concerns; and analyzes the institutional conditions relevant to its governance. Using a qualitative, non-experimental, exploratory-analytical design, the study draws on academic publications, policy documents, regulatory instruments, institutional guidelines, human-rights reports, and documented analyses of digital religious practices. Materials were purposively selected for substantive relevance and examined through structured reading and extraction, open and focused coding, thematic synthesis, source triangulation, and iterative cross-source comparison. The analysis identified three interconnected domains: access, visibility, and religious authority; religious freedom, inclusion, and algorithmic risks; and accountability, contestability, and institutional responsibility. AI-mediated technologies can broaden access to religious resources while simultaneously shaping the visibility and perceived authority of religious actors and interpretations. Expanded access can coexist with unequal representation, privacy risks, profiling, and constraints on meaningful participation, while distributed responsibility can create accountability gaps when consequential outcomes are difficult to explain or challenge. These relationships are context-dependent rather than predetermined effects of AI. By integrating sociotechnical and algorithmic-governance perspectives, the study provides an analytical framework for understanding ethical governance as the intersection of technological mediation, religious pluralism, fundamental rights, participation, and identifiable institutional responsibility.

items.abstract: This research reveals the contemporary British fiction crisis of human identity through a comparative reading of Kazoo Ishiguro’s Klara and the Sun and Ian McEwan’s Machines Like Me. Both novels view artificial intelligence as more than just a technology, instead, they treat it as a tool for subverting the human-machine divide. According to Adam, humans do not possess true moral agency, while Klara brings into question the nature of love, care, memory, and social recognition as essential qualities of personhood. By drawing upon the frameworks of critical posthumanism and AI ethics, we can find out that the novels are more concerned with whether human beings are capable of retaining a stable and exceptional identity when affect, consciousness, simulation, and ethical agency become entangled rather than on whether machines can be human. As comparison shows that artifice operates as a mirror through which contemporary fiction exhibits the ethical, emotional and ontological fragility of the human self.

items.title: Artificial intelligence applied to formulation design, process optimization, and quality assessment of 3D-printed dosage forms and drug-delivery systems: a scoping review
items.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) printing is a computer-aided, layer-by-layer manufacturing technology with strong potential for personalized medicines. Combined with artificial intelligence (AI), it enables predictive, data-driven development, improving formulation design, process robustness, and quality control. However, evidence remains fragmented across technologies, dosage forms, and computational approaches. This scoping review aimed to map and describe the application of AI to formulation design, manufacturing-process optimization, and quality assessment of pharmaceutical dosage forms and drug-delivery systems produced by 3D printing, including device-assisted delivery systems such as microneedles. The review followed Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Searches were conducted in MEDLINE/PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science until November 18, 2025. Original studies applying AI to the design, manufacturing, or quality assessment of 3D-printed drug products or drug–device combinations were included. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and analysis. Findings were synthesized through descriptive tables and narrative analysis. Twenty studies published between 2020 and 2025 met the inclusion criteria. Technologies included Fused Deposition Modeling, Selective Laser Sintering, Semi-Solid Extrusion, Vat Photopolymerization, and Inkjet Printing. Oral dosage forms and associated formulation or printing workflows predominated; two studies specifically investigated microneedle-based delivery systems. Reported approaches included random forests, support vector machines, artificial neural networks, deep learning, chemometric regression, generative models, Bayesian optimization, and evolutionary algorithms. Applications addressed formulation and printability prediction, processing-condition selection, drug-release modeling, and image-based quality assessment. Individual studies reported potential benefits related to process robustness, experimental effort, and development time; however, differences in study designs, datasets, and outcome definitions limit comparisons and generalization. The review maps applications of AI in formulation design, process optimization, and quality assessment in pharmaceutical 3D printing, without establishing their comparative effectiveness. Future research should prioritize methodological harmonization, standardized validation, and interdisciplinary collaboration to facilitate translation and regulatory acceptance.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence as a Tool for Addressing Real-World Challenges
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and data science are increasingly proposed as ways to extend scarce expertise, interpret complex data, and improve the timing and targeting of services in low- and middle-income countries and other resource-constrained communities. This paper synthesizes recent peer-reviewed studies and institutional guidance across education, healthcare, humanitarian assistance, disaster response, agriculture, and public information management. Evidence shows that carefully bounded systems can perform useful tasks: offline crop-disease screening can assist extension workers; AI-supported diabetic-retinopathy screening can expand diagnostic capacity; machine-learning forecasts can support flood warnings; and data-driven poverty maps or mobile-phone signals can inform social-assistance targeting. Yet predictive accuracy is not equivalent to public benefit. Benefits depend on representative data, local validation, affordable and resilient infrastructure, accessible interfaces, trusted institutions, and human capacity to act on outputs. Comparative evidence is strongest for specific, measurable tasks and substantially weaker for long-term population outcomes and scalable implementation. Major risks include exclusion of people poorly represented in data, proxy-label bias, privacy and surveillance harms, automation overreach, weak redress, and dependence on external platforms. The paper argues for locally led, task-specific, human-accountable AI, evaluated against non-AI alternatives and real service outcomes. It concludes with a research agenda centered on data stewardship, context-sensitive evaluation, accessible deployment, and equitable governance.

items.title: Artificial intelligence for sustainable power systems applications challenges and future directions
items.abstract: Abstract Stretching the integration of renewable energy, energy storage, electric vehicles (EVs) and smart-grid technologies at an unprecedented rate will produce increasingly complex and dynamic power systems that defy conventional optimization and control methods. This paper offers a systematic engineering review of the state of the art and future potential for the application of artificial intelligence (AI) in sustainable and resilient electric power systems, which includes machine learning, deep learning, reinforcement learning (RL), hybrid AI, explainable artificial intelligence, federated learning (FL), and digital twins (DTs). The review covers their use in renewable energy and load forecasting, energy management, predictive maintenance, demand response, adaptive control, energy storage, smart grid and EV/Vehicle-to-Grid coordination. A single framework based on the grid is presented that integrates predictive intelligence, optimization, adaptive control, cyber-physical systems, explainability, cyber-security, and sustainability in a closed-loop system. The analysis underscores the transformative possibilities of AI in enhancing the use of renewable energy, its efficiency, resilience of the grid and smart decision making. But, deployment needs to address the uncertainties, data quality, computational costs, latency, Cybersecurity, interoperability, scalability, model drift, and regulatory needs. The review also highlights Green AI to tackle the energy and carbon footprint of increasingly large AI models. Lastly, physics-informed and uncertainty-aware AI, safe RL, DT-assisted validation, edge intelligence, FL and real-world benchmarking are identified as key directions for next-generation power systems to remain trustworthy and sustainable.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Breast Cancer Diagnosis, Treatment, and Perioperative Management: A Systematic Review of Current Applications and Future Perspectives.
items.abstract: Background: Breast cancer is the most frequently diagnosed malignancy in women globally, accounting for approximately 2.30 million new cases and 666,103 deaths in 2022. Artificial intelligence technologies including machine learning, deep learning, radiomics, and natural language processing have been widely applied across the breast cancer care continuum. However, no systematic review restricted to primary studies with patient-level or image-level data has synthesized evidence spanning all clinical domains simultaneously. Objectives: To evaluate the performance, methodological quality, and clinical relevance of artificial intelligence primary studies across screening and diagnostic imaging, digital pathology, radiomics, perioperative management, prognostic prediction, and natural language processing in breast cancer. Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from January 2015 to May 2026. Eligibility was restricted to original primary research reporting patient-level or image-level data; secondary syntheses were explicitly excluded. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2 and PROBAST. Reporting followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Results: Of 5,275 identified records, 17 primary studies met eligibility criteria. In screening mammography (seven studies; n = 7,540 to 144,231 examinations), deep learning achieved area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values of 0.876 to 0.939; a randomised trial in 80,033 women demonstrated non-inferiority to double reading with a 44.3% reduction in radiologist workload. In digital pathology (five studies; 270 to 44,732 whole-slide images), deep learning achieved AUC 0.985 to 0.994, exceeding unassisted pathologist performance in lymph node metastasis detection. Magnetic resonance imaging radiomics predicted pathological complete response in HER2-positive breast cancer with AUC 0.80. No breast cancer-specific perioperative primary study met the eligibility criteria. Deep survival networks achieved concordance index 0.626 versus 0.612 for Cox regression in breast cancer cohorts. Natural language processing identified metastatic recurrence in breast cancer clinical records with sensitivity 83% and specificity 73%. Risk of bias was low to moderate for imaging and pathology studies and high for small sample radiomics studies. Density-stratified performance was reported by only two imaging studies, and receptor status prediction from haematoxylin and eosin staining had not been validated as a safe alternative to immunohistochemistry. Conclusions: Artificial intelligence demonstrated clinically meaningful performance across the five domains with eligible primary studies. Breast cancer-specific perioperative and intensive care primary studies were absent, representing the largest evidence gap. External validation, demographic diversity, and prospective clinical integration evidence remained the most consistently identified limitations. Prediction of molecular receptor status without immunohistochemistry requires rigorous prospective safety validation before it can complement standard testing.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Economic Forecasting: Applications in Inflation Prediction and Macroeconomic Analysis
items.abstract: This paper examines how artificial intelligence (AI), particularly statistical machine learning (ML), can complement established econometric approaches to inflation forecasting and macroeconomic analysis. Inflation is a difficult prediction target because it is measured with delay, revised in some datasets, driven by multiple interacting forces, and subject to structural change. Linear time-series and structural models remain valuable because they encode persistence, economic mechanisms, and interpretable scenarios. ML methods can add value where information sets are wide, relationships are nonlinear, interactions matter, or data arrive in mixed formats. The central question is therefore not whether Al replaces econometrics, but when and under what validation conditions it improves a policy-relevant forecast. A literature-based synthesis reviews foundational inflation forecasting research, contemporary ML studies, central-bank applications, and institutional data sources. The evidence is conditional. Data-rich ML models improved on selected benchmarks in a prominent U.S. application, yet later replications found that relative performance changes across countries, benchmarks, methods, and episodes. An ECB quantile-regression-forest application found small advantages for core inflation but mixed results for headline inflation. Text embeddings of central-bank communication have also shown forecast information in one euro-area application, although this remains specialized evidence. Broader IMF and OECD studies on output growth and GDP nowcasting are discussed as adjacent, not direct, inflation evidence.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Higher Education: The Role of Fairness, Transparency, and Accountability in Student Acceptance
items.abstract: This study examined the influence of Fairness, Transparency, and Accountability [FTA] on student acceptance of Artificial Intelligence [AI] in higher education institutions in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. Grounded on an extended Technology Acceptance Model, data were collected from 240 undergraduate students from six universities using a structured 5-point likert scale questionnaire. Descriptive analysis and Pearson correlation were conducted using SPSS v26. Results indicated that students reported moderately high acceptance of AI for learning but low perceptions of fairness, transparency, and accountability. Transparency emerged as the most critical concern, with 45-50% of students reporting limited understanding of AI decision-making processes. Correlation analysis revealed significant positive relationships between all three FTA dimensions and student acceptance. The findings suggest that while perceived usefulness drives initial adoption, ethical concerns may hinder sustainable use. The study recommends that Pakistani HEIs implement bias-free AI systems, provide explainable AI interfaces, and establish clear accountability structures to build student trust. This study contributes to AI ethics literature in the Pakistani context and provides implications for policymakers and university administrators.

items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly reshaping customer engagement, yet its influence on consumer behavior within hospitality and tourism services remains underexplored.This study examines the associations among AI-enabled engagement, digital marketing, and consumer behavior in hospitality and tourism contexts.Survey data were collected from 221 respondents and analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) in an exploratory capacity.The measurement analysis revealed that AI, digital marketing, and consumer behavior are very strongly interrelated: inter-construct correlations were high (AI-DM r = 0.871; DM-CB r = 0.882) and exceeded the square roots of the average variance extracted, so the three constructs did not achieve discriminant validity under the Fornell-Larcker criterion.Rather than interpreting this as a mediation mechanism, the study treats it as a substantive finding: in this hospitality and tourism setting, consumers appear to experience AI, the digital marketing it enables, and their own engagement responses as a single, tightly coupled digitalengagement domain rather than as separable constructs.Model fit was marginal (RMSEA = 0.113; CFI = 0.870), so all relationships are reported as indicative and associational rather than causal.The study contributes contextually by situating AI within hospitality and tourism service ecosystems and by documenting the strong convergence of these digital-engagement constructs, offering guidance for hospitality organizations and advancing discourse on sustainable, human-centered tourism strategies aligned with logistics, informatics, and service science.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Infertility Management: A Narrative Review of Current Evidence
items.abstract: In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) has become a powerful tool in various aspects of our daily lives. One of the most particular areas revolutionized by AI is medicine. Reproductive medicine is no exception to this integration. A narrative review was conducted to evaluate the current applications of AI-powered tools in the management of infertility. Searches were performed on October 25th, 2025, in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, Embase, Cochrane Library, and IEEE Xplore using predefined keywords and Boolean operators. After duplicate removal, screening, and eligibility assessment, original English-language studies relevant to AI-assisted infertility management were included for analysis. Our search identified 18 studies published between 2013 and 2025. Embryo selection and implantation prediction in in vitro fertilization (IVF) and intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) were the most common applications (8 studies), with AI models demonstrating superior performance compared to embryologists in several studies. The STORK deep neural network also demonstrated high accuracy in blastocyst quality assessment, while machine learning models showed promise in predicting ovarian reserve and fertilization outcomes. Other applications included ovarian stimulation optimization (3 studies), male infertility assessment (2 studies), and broader reproductive outcomes including live birth and miscarriage prediction (5 studies). AI shows promising potential to support infertility management by improving embryo selection, ovarian stimulation, assessment of male infertility, and broader reproductive outcomes. To ensure safe clinical adoption, future work must prioritize multi-center prospective trials, transparency, and standardized frameworks.

items.abstract: This study aims to analyse the existing literature and identify major research trends in artificial intelligence in logistics service quality research.Data were retrieved from the Scopus database, comprising 281 journal articles and review papers published between 2002 and 2026, after applying predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria to an initial dataset of 533 records.A bibliometric analysis was conducted using R Studio (Bibliometrix/Biblioshiny) and VOSviewer to examine publication trends, citation patterns, influential sources, country productivity, highly cited documents, keyword co-occurrence networks, and thematic structures within the research domain.The findings indicate a rapidly expanding body of research linking artificial intelligence and digital technologies with logistics service quality, customer satisfaction, e-commerce logistics, last-mile delivery, route optimization, and digital supply chain management.The field has experienced particularly strong growth after 2020, reaching its highest publication output in 2025.Customer satisfaction emerges as the most central keyword, suggesting that the literature remains strongly grounded in a service-quality and customer-experience perspective, even as advanced technologies such as artificial intelligence, machine learning, big data analytics, the Internet of Things, blockchain, automation, and optimization techniques become increasingly integrated into logistics service systems.Keyword co-occurrence analysis and thematic mapping are used as two complementary techniques.The keyword co-occurrence analysis identifies four major clusters representing distinct research streams, while thematic mapping reveals five thematic areas, reflecting different analytical logics underlying network-based clustering and centralitydensity-based classification.The study contributes to a clearer understanding of the intellectual structure of AI-driven logistics service quality research and provides future research directions related to customer experience, sustainable last-mile delivery, responsible AI adoption, and intelligent logistics service systems.
